options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer that has one HTTPS listener on port 80. Attach an SSL/TLS certificate to listener port 80. Create a rule to redirect requests from HTTP to HTTPS.

Create an Application Load Balancer that has one HTTP listener on port 80 and one HTTPS protocol listener on port 443. Attach an SSL/TLS certificate to listener port 443. Create a rule to redirect requests from port 80 to port 443.

Create an Application Load Balancer that has two TCP listeners on port 80 and port 443. Attach an SSL/TLS certificate to listener port 443. Create a rule to redirect requests from port 80 to port 443.
Create a Network Load Balancer that has two TCP listeners on port 80 and port 443. Attach an SSL/TLS certificate to listener port 443. Create a rule to redirect requests from port 80 to port 443.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer can use an ACM certificate on an HTTPS listener and can redirect requests received by an HTTP listener on port 80 to HTTPS on port 443. This provides TLS termination for the public website while enforcing HTTPS for clients.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for your Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-listeners.html) · [Security Hub CSPM controls for Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/elb-controls.html)

A CloudOps engineer is reviewing the following AWS CloudFormation template:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783910525039-gxl99mwu.png)  
  
Why does creation of the stack fail?

options.text: The Outputs section of the CloudFormation template was omitted.
The Parameters section of the CloudFormation template was omitted.
The PrivateDnsName cannot be sot from a CloudFormation template.
The VPC was not specified in the CloudFormation template.

questions.explanation:
`PrivateDnsName` is not a supported configurable property of `AWS::EC2::Instance`; it is a read-only resource attribute that can be retrieved with `Fn::GetAtt`. The supported instance setting for hostname behavior is `PrivateDnsNameOptions`, so specifying `PrivateDnsName` in `Properties` causes CloudFormation validation to fail.

**Learn more:** [AWS::EC2::Instance - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-instance.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is implementing Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for its Amazon S3 buckets. The S3 buckets are in the `us-east-1` Region. The company uses server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) to protect the data in the buckets.  
  
A CloudOps engineer creates a new AWS account to store backups in S3 buckets. All backup buckets are in the `us-west-2` Region. The CloudOps engineer enables versioning on both the source buckets and destination buckets. The CloudOps engineer creates an IAM role in the source account for `s3.amazonaws.com`. The CloudOps engineer grants the IAM role permissions to perform read actions in the source buckets, replicate actions in the destination buckets, and encrypt actions using the destination bucket's key. The destination bucket policy allows the IAM role to perform replicate and read actions.  
  
After completing the replication configuration, the CloudOps engineer notices that objects are not replicating.  
  
What is the likely reason that the objects are not replicating?

options.text: The IAM role and bucket policies must have the ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner permission.
The objects in the source buckets and destination buckets must be encrypted by multi-Region keys.
Gateway VPC endpoints for Amazon S3 must be created in the source accounts and the destination account.
The destination buckets must use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

questions.explanation:
When cross-account replication is configured to transfer replica ownership to the destination bucket owner, the S3 replication role and the destination bucket policy must allow `s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner`. SSE-S3 supports replication and does not require multi-Region KMS keys or SSE-KMS at the destination, and S3 replication does not require gateway VPC endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting replication - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-troubleshoot.html) · [Changing the replica owner - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-change-owner.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer needs to create an IAM policy for a developer who requires access to particular AWS services. Based on these requirements, the CloudOps engineer creates the following policy:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783925911740-zb3eut1x.png)  
  
Which actions are allowed by this policy? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway.
Create an IAM role for an AWS Lambda function.
Delete an Amazon SQS queue.
Describe AWS load balancers.
Invoke an AWS Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
The policy allows all Elastic Load Balancing actions through `elasticloadbalancing:*`, which includes `DescribeLoadBalancers`, and all AWS Lambda actions through `lambda:*`, which includes `InvokeFunction`. It does not allow Storage Gateway creation, IAM role creation, or SQS queue deletion because those actions do not match the permitted action patterns.

**Learn more:** [How Elastic Load Balancing works with IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html) · [Actions, resources, and condition keys for AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_awslambda.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer created a VPC containing a public subnet and a private subnet. Amazon EC2 instances launched in the private subnet cannot reach the internet. The default network ACL is active for every subnet in the VPC, and every security group permits all outbound traffic.  
  
Which solution will give the EC2 instances in the private subnet internet access?

options.text: Create a NAT gateway in the public subnet. Create a route from the private subnet to the NAT gateway.
Create a NAT gateway in the public subnet. Create a route from the public subnet to the NAT gateway.
Create a NAT gateway in the private subnet. Create a route from the public subnet to the NAT gateway.
Create a NAT gateway in the private subnet. Create a route from the private subnet to the NAT gateway.

questions.explanation:
A NAT gateway placed in a public subnet provides outbound internet connectivity for instances that have only private IP addresses. The private subnet’s route table must direct internet-bound traffic to that NAT gateway; the NAT gateway uses the public subnet’s route to the internet gateway.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html) · [Subnet route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/subnet-route-tables.html)

A CloudOps engineer has successfully deployed a VPC by using an AWS CloudFormation template. The CloudOps engineer needs to deploy that same template across multiple accounts managed through AWS Organizations.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Assume the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role from the management account. Deploy the template in each of the accounts.
Create an AWS Lambda function to assume a role in each account. Deploy the template by using the AWS CloudFormation CreateStack API call.
Create an AWS Lambda function to query for a list of accounts. Deploy the template by using the AWS CloudFormation CreateStack API call.
Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets from the management account to deploy the template in each of the accounts.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation StackSets centrally deploys and manages the same CloudFormation template across multiple AWS accounts. When used with AWS Organizations service-managed permissions, CloudFormation automatically creates and manages the required roles in member accounts, eliminating per-account deployments and custom Lambda automation.

**Learn more:** [Managing stacks across accounts and Regions with StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html) · [Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-orgs-associate-stackset-with-org.html)

A CloudOps engineer needs to troubleshoot performance problems for a web application delivered through Amazon CloudFront. Metrics show a consistently low cache hit ratio, causing many requests to be forwarded to the origin.  
  
Which configuration will increase the cache hit ratio?

options.text: Modify the origin's Cache-Control header to max-age=0.
Reduce the TTL for cached objects.
Reduce the number of request headers, query strings, and cookies included in the cache key.
Configure signed URLs or signed cookies to restrict access to content.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront uses the cache key to determine whether a request matches a valid cached object. Including only the minimum necessary request headers, query strings, and cookies reduces cache-key variation, increasing the likelihood of cache hits and reducing origin requests.

**Learn more:** [Understand the cache key - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/understanding-the-cache-key.html) · [Control the cache key with a policy - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/controlling-the-cache-key.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must monitor the availability of its website for end users. The company requires a solution that sends an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification when the website's uptime falls below 99%. The monitoring must deliver an accurate representation of the website user experience.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the website’s logs that are published to a CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure the alarm to publish an SNS notification if the number of HTTP 4xx errors and 5xx errors exceeds a specified threshold.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the website's published metrics in CloudWatch. Configure the alarm to publish an SNS notification that is based on anomaly detection.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics heartbeat monitoring canary. Associate the canary with the website's URL for end users. Create a CloudWatch alarm for the canary. Configure the alarm to publish an SNS notification if the value of the SuccessPercent metric is less than 99%.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics broken link checker monitoring canary. Associate the canary with the website's URL for end users. Create a CloudWatch alarm for the canary. Configure the alarm to publish an SNS notification if the value of the SuccessPercent metric is less than 99%.

questions.explanation:
CloudWatch Synthetics heartbeat canaries load a specified website URL on a schedule, simulating customer access and thereby measuring availability from the end-user perspective. Canaries publish the `SuccessPercent` metric, which is the percentage of successful canary runs; a CloudWatch alarm can trigger an Amazon SNS notification when that metric falls below 99%.

**Learn more:** [Using canary blueprints - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_Blueprints.html) · [CloudWatch metrics published by canaries - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_metrics.html)

questions.domain: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Systems Manager to automate tasks across AWS accounts. It uses monitoring tools to identify issues and creates a Systems Manager Automation runbook that runs an AWS Lambda function to remediate those issues.  
  
At first, the company runs the runbook manually. The company now wants the runbook to run automatically whenever its monitoring tools detect issues.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Configure the monitoring tools to publish findings to Amazon EventBridge. Create an EventBridge rule that invokes the runbook in response to events from the monitoring tools.
Configure the monitoring tools to send findings to an Amazon SNS topic. Subscribe the runbook to the SNS topic. Invoke the runbook when a message is received.
Configure the monitoring tools to write findings to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter that invokes the runbook when new log entries are detected.
Configure AWS Config to assess the resources and publish configuration changes to Amazon EventBridge. Create a rule to invoke the runbook in response to configuration change events.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge rules can use Systems Manager Automation as a target and start a runbook when an event matching the rule’s event pattern occurs. Having the monitoring tools publish their findings to EventBridge therefore provides an event-driven trigger for the remediation runbook.

**Learn more:** [Run automations based on EventBridge events - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/running-automations-event-bridge.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Automation - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-automation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates multiple Amazon EC2 instances that use the Ubuntu operating system (OS). The company must patch the OS on a regular basis. A CloudOps engineer manually installs patches each week. The company continually adds new EC2 instances running Ubuntu. The CloudOps engineer must automate the patching process.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to connect to the EC2 instances by using SSH and to install the patches. Configure the Lambda function to run every week.
Install the AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) on the EC2 instances. Configure Systems Manager Patch Manager to install patches on the instances every week.
Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to identify unpatched EC2 instances and to install OS patches.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that has a cron expression to install the patches every week. Configure the EventBridge rule to target the EC2 instances. Configure an action to run OS updates on the targeted instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates patch scanning and installation for managed EC2 instances, including Ubuntu Server nodes, and can run patch installation on a defined schedule. Installing the SSM Agent enables the instances to be managed without maintaining SSH-based custom automation. Patch Manager uses Ubuntu’s package-management workflow to apply approved patches, while Systems Manager Inventory is for collecting inventory and compliance information rather than installing patches.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html) · [How patches are installed - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-installing-patches.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer cannot launch Amazon EC2 instances into a VPC because the VPC has no available private IPv4 addresses.  
  
Which combination of actions must the CloudOps engineer perform to launch the instances? (Choose two.)

options.text: Associate a secondary IPv4 CIDR block with the VPC.
Associate a primary IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC.
Create a new subnet for the VPC.
Modify the CIDR block of the VPC.
Modify the CIDR block of the subnet that is associated with the instances.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 instance receives its primary private IPv4 address from the IPv4 address range of its subnet. Adding a secondary IPv4 CIDR block expands the VPC's IPv4 address space, and a new subnet can be created from that added CIDR block to supply available private IPv4 addresses. A subnet's IPv4 CIDR block cannot be changed after creation, and an IPv6 CIDR block does not provide the required private IPv4 addresses.

**Learn more:** [Add or remove a CIDR block from your VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/add-ipv4-cidr.html) · [IP addressing for your VPCs and subnets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-ip-addressing.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company operates a web application. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute traffic among multiple Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones. The application receives high traffic during flash sales. The company must ensure that requests are distributed evenly across all healthy instances. In addition, the company needs session persistence for shopping cart functionality.  
  
Which configuration satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative effort?

options.text: Configure the ALB target group to use the round robin algorithm. Enable stickiness and cross-zone load balancing.
Switch the ALB to a Network Load Balancer. Modify the target group to use the least outstanding requests algorithm. Enable stickiness. Disable cross-zone load balancing.
Configure the ALB target group to use the weighted round robin algorithm. Implement session persistence by using AWS Lambda functions to store session data in Amazon DynamoDB.

Configure the ALB listener with path-based routing to direct shopping cart requests to a dedicated target group with sticky sessions. Use the round robin algorithm without stickiness for a second target group.

questions.explanation:
Round robin routing on an ALB target group distributes requests evenly among healthy targets. Enabling target-group stickiness binds a client session to the initially selected target, preserving shopping-cart session continuity. Cross-zone load balancing enables load balancer nodes to distribute requests across registered healthy targets in all enabled Availability Zones. AWS does not support weighted-random routing together with sticky sessions.

**Learn more:** [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html) · [How Elastic Load Balancing works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operating multiple workloads on AWS wants to improve its security posture by implementing DNS-based threat protection. The company needs to block DNS-based attacks.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Shield Advanced to filter and block malicious DNS queries. Set up domain filtering policies.
Use AWS WAF to inspect DNS traffic for malicious domains. Create custom rules to block known threats.
Configure Amazon Route 53 Resolver to forward DNS queries to Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall Advanced to detect and filter threats.
Configure AWS Config to monitor DNS queries and DNS traffic patterns. Use an AWS Lambda function to prevent access to malicious domains.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall Advanced detects DNS threats, including DNS tunneling and domain-generation-algorithm (DGA) activity, and can apply a block action to matching DNS queries. It operates with Route 53 Resolver to filter outbound DNS queries from VPC workloads.

**Learn more:** [How Resolver DNS Firewall works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-dns-firewall-overview.html) · [DNS Firewall Advanced Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/firewall-advanced.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer used AWS CloudFormation to deploy a serverless application in a production VPC. The application includes an AWS Lambda function, an Amazon DynamoDB table, and an Amazon API Gateway API. The CloudOps engineer needs to delete the AWS CloudFormation stack while retaining the DynamoDB table.  
  
Which action should the CloudOps engineer perform before deleting the AWS CloudFormation stack?

options.text: Add a Retain deletion policy to the DynamoDB resource in the AWS CloudFormation stack.
Add a Snapshot deletion policy to the DynamoDB resource in the AWS CloudFormation stack.
Enable termination protection on the AWS CloudFormation stack.
Update the application's IAM policy with a Deny statement for the dynamodb:DeleteTable action.

questions.explanation:
A `DeletionPolicy` of `Retain` on the DynamoDB resource causes AWS CloudFormation to keep the physical table and its contents when the stack is deleted. The retained table is removed from CloudFormation management and continues to exist independently of the deleted stack.

**Learn more:** [AWS CloudFormation DeletionPolicy attribute](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company security policy requires that incoming SSH traffic be limited to a defined set of addresses. The company uses an AWS Config rule to determine whether security groups permit unrestricted incoming SSH traffic.  
  
A CloudOps engineer identifies a noncompliant resource and manually corrects the security group. The CloudOps engineer wants to automate remediation for other noncompliant resources.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the AWS Config rule's status metric. Create an AWS Lambda function that can remove the noncompliant rule from the security group. Configure the alarm action to invoke the Lambda function.
Configure an automatic remediation action on the AWS Config rule. Specify the AWS-DisablolncomingSSHOnPort22 remediation action.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule for AWS Config configuration item change events. Create an AWS Lambda function that can remove the noncompliant rule from the security groupConfigure the rule to invoke the Lambda function.

Create an AWS Lambda function that can analyze a security group’s inbound rules to check for unrestricted SSH access. Configure the Lambda function to remove the noncompliant rule from the security group. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every hour.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config can automatically remediate resources that its rules mark noncompliant by invoking an associated Systems Manager Automation remediation action. The AWS-managed `AWS-DisableIncomingSSHOnPort22` runbook removes unrestricted inbound SSH rules on TCP port 22 from security groups, directly enforcing the policy without custom Lambda code or separate CloudWatch/EventBridge automation.

**Learn more:** [Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/setup-autoremediation.html) · [AWS-DisableIncomingSSHOnPort22 runbook](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/disable-incoming-ssh.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an FTP server on Amazon EC2 instances. In the company’s AWS environment, AWS Security Hub sends findings about the EC2 instances to Amazon EventBridge because the FTP port has become publicly exposed in the security groups attached to the instances.  
  
A CloudOps engineer needs an automated solution to remediate the Security Hub finding and any similar findings for exposed ports. The CloudOps engineer wants to use an event-driven approach.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the existing EventBridge event to stop the EC2 instances that have the exposed port.

Create a cron job for the FTP server to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to modify the security group of the identified EC2 instances and to remove the instances that allow public access.
Create a cron job for the FTP server that invokes an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to modify the server to use SFTP instead of FTP.
Configure the existing EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the function to remove the security group rule that allows public access.

questions.explanation:
AWS Security Hub sends findings to EventBridge in near real time, and EventBridge rules can invoke AWS Lambda functions for automated remediation. A Lambda function can revoke the inbound security group rule that permits public access, eliminating the exposed-port condition while applying the same event-driven remediation pattern to similar findings.

**Learn more:** [Using EventBridge for automated response and remediation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-cloudwatch-events.html) · [Automatically modifying and acting on findings in Security Hub CSPM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/automations.html)

questions.domain: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company requires an AWS Lambda function to carry out a custom recovery procedure on the application server whenever the application returns an HTTP 500 status code.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must design a solution that detects HTTP 500 status codes and reliably runs the Lambda function when errors occur.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count ALB target group metric. Set the alarm action to run the Lambda function.
Deploy a new Lambda function that continuously scans the ALB access logs in Amazon S3 to detect HTTP 500 status codes and then invokes the existing lambda function.
Enable AWS CloudTrail on the application instances. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filters to detect HTTP 500 status codes and run the Lambda function.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for all ALB request events that invokes the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to filter for HTTP 500 status codes internally.

questions.explanation:
The `HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count` metric in the `AWS/ApplicationELB` namespace records HTTP 5xx response codes generated by ALB targets. A CloudWatch alarm can monitor this metric and invoke a Lambda function as its alarm action. CloudWatch alarms invoke Lambda asynchronously on the relevant alarm state change and retry if they cannot reach Lambda or the invocation is rejected, providing the required reliable trigger.

**Learn more:** [CloudWatch metrics for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html) · [Invoke a Lambda function from an alarm](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/alarms-and-actions-Lambda.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer needs to share a copy of a production database with a migration account. The production database runs on an Amazon RDS DB instance and is encrypted at rest using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias `production-rds-key`.  
  
What must the CloudOps engineer do to satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative overhead?

options.text: Take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance in the production account. Amend the KMS key policy of the production-rds-key KMS key to give access to the migration account’s root user. Share the snapshot with the migration account.
Create an RDS read replica in the migration account. Configure the KMS key policy to replicate the production-rds-key KMS key to the migration account.
Take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance in the production account. Share the snapshot with the migration account. In the migration account, create a new KMS key that has an identical alias.

Use native database toolsets to export the RDS DB instance to Amazon S3. Create an S3 bucket and an S3 bucket policy for cross-account access between the production account and the migration account. Use native database toolsets to import the database from Amazon S3 to a new RDS DB instance.

questions.explanation:
An encrypted Amazon RDS snapshot can be shared cross-account when it is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key and that key’s policy allows the target account to use it. Granting the migration account access to `production-rds-key` and sharing a manual snapshot uses the native RDS cross-account snapshot workflow. An identical KMS alias in the target account does not provide access to the source key, and export/import introduces unnecessary operational work.

**Learn more:** [Sharing encrypted snapshots for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/share-encrypted-snapshot.html) · [Sharing a DB snapshot for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ShareSnapshot.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer is responsible for the security and compliance of a company's AWS account. To make sure the company's Amazon EC2 instances comply with company policy, the CloudOps engineer wants to terminate every EC2 instance that lacks a department tag. Noncompliant resources must be terminated near real time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Config rule with the required-tags managed rule to identify noncompliant resources. Configure automatic remediation to run the AWS-TerminateEC2Instance automation runbook to terminate noncompliant resources.
Create a new Amazon EventBridge rule to monitor when new EC2 instances are created. Send the event to an Amazon SNS topic for automatic remediation.
Ensure all users who can create EC2 instances also have the permissions to use the ec2:CreateTags and ec2:DescribeTags actions. Change the instance's shutdown behavior to terminate.
Ensure AWS Systems Manager Compliance is configured to manage the EC2 instances. Call the AWS-StopEC2Instances automation runbook to stop noncompliant resources.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Config `required-tags` managed rule supports `AWS::EC2::Instance` and identifies instances missing a configured tag key. Config rules can use automatic Systems Manager Automation remediation for noncompliant resources, and the `AWS-TerminateEC2Instance` runbook terminates the identified EC2 instance.

**Learn more:** [required-tags - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/required-tags.html) · [Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/setup-autoremediation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its production file server to AWS. All data stored on the file server must remain accessible if an Availability Zone becomes unavailable or during system maintenance. Users must be able to interact with the file server by using the SMB protocol. Users must also be able to manage file permissions by using Windows ACLs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a single AWS Storage Gateway file gateway.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system.
Deploy two AWS Storage Gateway file gateways across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the file gateways.
Deploy two Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Single-AZ 2 file systems Configure Microsoft Distributed File System Replication (DFSR).

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ provides SMB access and supports standard Windows ACLs for file- and folder-level access control. Its Windows file-server cluster spans two Availability Zones and automatically fails over to a standby server during an Availability Zone outage or planned maintenance, preserving access to the file system.

**Learn more:** [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html) · [File- and folder-level access control using Windows ACLs - Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/limit-access-file-folder.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An environment contains 100 Amazon EC2 Windows instances. The Amazon CloudWatch agent is deployed and running on every EC2 instance with a baseline configuration file that captures log files. A new requirement is to capture the DHCP log files that are present on 50 of the instances.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient way to fulfill this new requirement?

options.text: Create an additional CloudWatch agent configuration filo to capture the DHCP logs. Use the AWS Systems Manager Run Command to restart the CloudWatch agent on each EC2 instance with the append-config option to apply the additional configuration file.
Log in to each EC2 instance with administrator rights. Create a PowerShell script to push the needed baseline log files and DHCP log files to CloudWatch.
Run the CloudWatch agent configuration file wizard on each EC2 instance. Verify that the baseline log files are included and add the DHCP log files during the wizard creation process.
Run the CloudWatch agent configuration file wizard on each EC2 instance and select the advanced detail level. This will capture the operating system log files.

questions.explanation:
The CloudWatch agent supports multiple configuration files on Windows Server. A separate configuration that collects DHCP logs can be appended to the existing baseline configuration, so both sets of logs are collected without replacing the baseline. AWS Systems Manager Run Command enables the agent configuration update and restart to be performed remotely across the applicable instances at scale.

**Learn more:** [Create the CloudWatch agent configuration file](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/create-cloudwatch-agent-configuration-file.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer is investigating a failed AWS CloudFormation stack creation. Before the CloudOps engineer can determine the issue, the stack and its resources are deleted. For future deployments, the CloudOps engineer must retain any resources that CloudFormation creates successfully.  
  
What should the CloudOps engineer do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Set the value of the DisableRollback parameter to False during stack creation.
Set the value of the OnFailure parameter to DO_NOTHING during stack creation.
Specify a rollback configuration that has a rollback trigger of DO_NOTHING during stack creation
Set the value of the OnFailure parameter to ROLLBACK during stack creation.

questions.explanation:
Setting the `OnFailure` parameter to `DO_NOTHING` prevents CloudFormation from automatically rolling back a failed stack-creation operation. Successfully created resources remain available, along with the failed stack's events, for troubleshooting.

**Learn more:** [AWS CloudFormation: Choose how to handle failures when provisioning resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stack-failure-options.html) · [AWS CloudFormation CreateStack API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/APIReference/API_CreateStack.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an internal web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group within a single Availability Zone. A CloudOps engineer must make the application highly available.  
  
Which action should the CloudOps engineer take to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Increase the maximum number of instances in the Auto Scaling group to meet the capacity that is required at peak usage.
Increase the minimum number of instances in the Auto Scaling group to meet the capacity that is required at peak usage.
Update the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances in a second Availability Zone in the same AWS Region.
Update the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances in an Availability Zone in a second AWS Region.

questions.explanation:
High availability across an Availability Zone failure requires instances in more than one Availability Zone. An Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones can launch replacement instances in an unaffected zone, while the load balancer distributes traffic to healthy targets. Increasing capacity within one Availability Zone does not protect against a zonal outage.

**Learn more:** [Add an Availability Zone - Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html) · [Resilience in Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing across multiple AWS Regions to provide resiliency. Route 53 latency-based routing directs traffic to the nearest Region. Within every Region, weighted A records distribute traffic across multiple Availability Zones.  
  
During a recent update, some Availability Zone endpoints became unhealthy, but Route 53 continued routing traffic to those unhealthy endpoints. The company must prevent this issue in the future.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Add a Route 53 health check for each of the weighted records that received traffic during the recent update.
Increase the weight of Route 53 records in the Region where traffic must go during updates.
Reconfigure all records to use latency-based routing across all Regions uniformly.
Reduce the TTL value for latency-based routing to detect changes more quickly.

questions.explanation:
Route 53 health checks can be associated with weighted records so that unhealthy endpoint records are not returned in DNS responses. This allows traffic to be directed only to healthy Availability Zone endpoints while retaining the existing latency-based regional routing and weighted distribution.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide — Configuring DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is implementing security and compliance using AWS Trusted Advisor. The company’s CloudOps team is validating the list of Trusted Advisor checks it can access.  
  
Which factor affects the number of available Trusted Advisor checks?

options.text: Whether at least ono Amazon EC2 instance is in the running state
The AWS Support plan
An AWS Organizations service control policy (SCP)
Whether the AWS account root user has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled

questions.explanation:
The AWS Support plan determines Trusted Advisor check availability. Basic and Developer Support plans have access to Service Limits checks and only selected Security and Fault Tolerance checks, while AWS Business Support+, AWS Enterprise Support, and AWS Unified Operations plans provide access to all Trusted Advisor checks.

**Learn more:** [AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/trusted-advisor.html) · [Organizational view for AWS Trusted Advisor](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/organizational-view.html)

options.text: Create an Aurora Replica. Promote the replica to replace the primary DB instance.
Create an AWS Lambda function to restore an automatic backup to the existing DB cluster.
Use backtracking to rewind the existing DB cluster to the desired recovery point.
Use point-in-time recovery to restore the existing DB duster to the desired recovery point.

questions.explanation:
Aurora MySQL Backtrack rewinds the existing DB cluster to a specified recovery time without restoring from a backup. The maximum backtrack window is 72 hours. Point-in-time recovery restores data by creating a new DB cluster, so it does not satisfy an in-place production-cluster rollback requirement.

**Learn more:** [Backtracking an Aurora DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Managing.Backtrack.html) · [Overview of backing up and restoring an Aurora DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Backups.html)

A company has scientists who upload large data objects to an Amazon S3 bucket using multipart uploads. These multipart uploads frequently fail because of poor end-client connectivity.  
  
The company wants to optimize the storage costs associated with the data. A CloudOps engineer must implement a solution that displays metrics for incomplete uploads and automatically deletes any incomplete uploads after 7 days.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Review the Incomplete Multipart Upload Bytes metric in the S3 Storage Lens dashboard. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to automatically delete any incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.
Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering to move data into lower-cost storage classes after 7 days. Create an S3 Storage Lens policy to automatically delete any incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.

Access the S3 console. Review the Metrics tab to check the storage that incomplete multipart uploads are consuming. Create an AWS Lambda function to delete any incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.

Use the S3 analytics storage class analysis tool to identify and measure incomplete multipart uploads. Configure an S3 bucket policy to enforce restrictions on multipart uploads to delete incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Storage Lens exposes the Incomplete Multipart Upload Bytes metric to report storage consumed by incomplete multipart uploads. An S3 Lifecycle rule using `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` can abort incomplete uploads after 7 days, deleting their uploaded parts and eliminating the associated storage cost. [Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics glossary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_metrics_glossary.html) [Multipart upload overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html)

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics glossary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_metrics_glossary.html) · [Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a VPC that includes a public subnet and a private subnet. The company deploys an Amazon EC2 instance in the private subnet using an Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI), with the AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) installed. The EC2 instance belongs to a security group that permits outbound traffic only.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must enable a group of privileged administrators to connect to the instance through SSH without exposing the instance to the internet.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Create an EC2 Instance Connect endpoint in the private subnet. Update the security group to allow inbound SSH traffic. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group.

Create a Systems Manager endpoint in the private subnet. Update the security group to allow SSH traffic from the private network where the Systems Manager endpoint is connected. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group.

Create an EC2 Instance Connect endpoint in the public subnet. Update the security group to allow SSH traffic from the private network. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group.

Create a Systems Manager endpoint in the public subnet. Create an IAM role that has the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore permission for the EC2 instance. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess IAM policy to the IAM group.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint provides an identity-aware private TCP proxy for connecting to instances that do not have public IP addresses. The endpoint’s security group must be allowed to reach the destination instance, so permitting inbound SSH to the instance from the endpoint enables SSH without internet exposure. EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint access is governed through IAM permissions, and PowerUserAccess grants broad access to EC2 capabilities. [Connect to your instances using a private IP address and EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/connect-with-ec2-instance-connect-endpoint.html)

**Learn more:** [Connect to your instances using a private IP address and EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/connect-with-ec2-instance-connect-endpoint.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html)

A CloudOps engineer must configure a caching layer for a read-heavy application that uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The application is deployed across three AWS Regions. Read and write operations take place in the primary Region. In the two secondary Regions, only read activity occurs on RDS for PostgreSQL cross-Region read replicas.  
  
The cache in every Region must contain the same data to ensure a consistent user experience across Regions.  
  
Which caching-layer solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Set up an Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) global datastore. Include a read and write cluster in the primary Region. Include a read-only cluster in each secondary Region.
Set up an Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached) global database. Include a read and write cluster in the primary Region. Include a read-only cluster in each secondary Region.
Set up query caching on the RDS for PostgreSQL database in the primary Region. Configure query cache replication to the secondary RDS cross-Region replicas.
Set up an Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached) cluster with cluster mode enabled in all three Regions. Set up ElastiCache cross-Region replication from the primary Region to the secondary Regions.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore for Redis OSS provides a writable primary cluster and read-only secondary clusters in other AWS Regions, with automatic cross-Region replication from the primary to the secondary clusters. This supplies local read caches in the secondary Regions while keeping their cached data replicated from the primary Region. Global Datastore is not available for ElastiCache Memcached.

**Learn more:** [Replication across AWS Regions using global datastores — Amazon ElastiCache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Redis-Global-Datastore.html) · [CreateGlobalReplicationGroup — Amazon ElastiCache API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/APIReference/API_CreateGlobalReplicationGroup.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a critical serverless application that uses multiple AWS Lambda functions. Each Lambda function produces 1 GB of log data per day in its own Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. The company’s security team requests a count of application errors, grouped by type, across all log groups.  
  
What should a CloudOps engineer do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Perform a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that uses the stats command and count function.
Perform a CloudWatch Logs search that uses the groupby keyword and count function.
Perform an Amazon Athena query that uses the SELECT and GROUP BV keywords.
Perform an Amazon RDS query that uses the SELECT and GROUP BY keywords.

questions.explanation:
CloudWatch Logs Insights can query multiple log groups and aggregate the matching log events. The `stats` command supports `count()` and grouping by a field, so it can return the count of application errors for each error type across the selected Lambda log groups.

**Learn more:** [stats - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL_QuerySyntax-Stats.html) · [Tutorial: Run a query with an aggregation function - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL_AnalyzeLogData_AggregationQuery.html)

51:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company has scientists who upload large data objects to an Amazon S3 bucket using multipart uploads. These multipart uploads frequently fail because of poor end-client connectivity."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to optimize the storage costs associated with the data. A CloudOps engineer must implement a solution that displays metrics for incomplete uploads and automatically deletes any incomplete uploads after 7 days."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Review the Incomplete Multipart Upload Bytes metric in the S3 Storage Lens dashboard. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to automatically delete any incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.","B":"Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering to move data into lower-cost storage classes after 7 days. Create an S3 Storage Lens policy to automatically delete any incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.","C":"Access the S3 console. Review the Metrics tab to check the storage that incomplete multipart uploads are consuming. Create an AWS Lambda function to delete any incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days.","D":"Use the S3 analytics storage class analysis tool to identify and measure incomplete multipart uploads. Configure an S3 bucket policy to enforce restrictions on multipart uploads to delete incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon S3 Storage Lens exposes the Incomplete Multipart Upload Bytes metric to report storage consumed by incomplete multipart uploads. An S3 Lifecycle rule using `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` can abort incomplete uploads after 7 days, deleting their uploaded parts and eliminating the associated storage cost. [Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics glossary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_metrics_glossary.html) [Multipart upload overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html)

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics glossary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_metrics_glossary.html) · [Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"73892029-8fb3-4d03-937c-680dd528708e","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-cloudops-engineer-associate-soa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company has a VPC that includes a public subnet and a private subnet. The company deploys an Amazon EC2 instance in the private subnet using an Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI), with the AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) installed. The EC2 instance belongs to a security group that permits outbound traffic only."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"A CloudOps engineer must enable a group of privileged administrators to connect to the instance through SSH without exposing the instance to the internet."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets this requirement?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an EC2 Instance Connect endpoint in the private subnet. Update the security group to allow inbound SSH traffic. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group.","B":"Create a Systems Manager endpoint in the private subnet. Update the security group to allow SSH traffic from the private network where the Systems Manager endpoint is connected. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group.","C":"Create an EC2 Instance Connect endpoint in the public subnet. Update the security group to allow SSH traffic from the private network. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the IAM group.","D":"Create a Systems Manager endpoint in the public subnet. Create an IAM role that has the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore permission for the EC2 instance. Create an IAM group for privileged administrators. Assign the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess IAM policy to the IAM group."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"An EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint provides an identity-aware private TCP proxy for connecting to instances that do not have public IP addresses. The endpoint’s security group must be allowed to reach the destination instance, so permitting inbound SSH to the instance from the endpoint enables SSH without internet exposure. EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint access is governed through IAM permissions, and PowerUserAccess grants broad access to EC2 capabilities. [Connect to your instances using a private IP address and EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/connect-with-ec2-instance-connect-endpoint.html)

**Learn more:** [Connect to your instances using a private IP address and EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/connect-with-ec2-instance-connect-endpoint.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"0e17324a-7ec5-4575-a7a4-a213ecd6b1d7","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-cloudops-engineer-associate-soa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A CloudOps engineer must configure a caching layer for a read-heavy application that uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The application is deployed across three AWS Regions. Read and write operations take place in the primary Region. In the two secondary Regions, only read activity occurs on RDS for PostgreSQL cross-Region read replicas."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The cache in every Region must contain the same data to ensure a consistent user experience across Regions."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which caching-layer solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Set up an Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS) global datastore. Include a read and write cluster in the primary Region. Include a read-only cluster in each secondary Region.","B":"Set up an Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached) global database. Include a read and write cluster in the primary Region. Include a read-only cluster in each secondary Region.","C":"Set up query caching on the RDS for PostgreSQL database in the primary Region. Configure query cache replication to the secondary RDS cross-Region replicas.","D":"Set up an Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached) cluster with cluster mode enabled in all three Regions. Set up ElastiCache cross-Region replication from the primary Region to the secondary Regions."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore for Redis OSS provides a writable primary cluster and read-only secondary clusters in other AWS Regions, with automatic cross-Region replication from the primary to the secondary clusters. This supplies local read caches in the secondary Regions while keeping their cached data replicated from the primary Region. Global Datastore is not available for ElastiCache Memcached.

**Learn more:** [Replication across AWS Regions using global datastores — Amazon ElastiCache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/Redis-Global-Datastore.html) · [CreateGlobalReplicationGroup — Amazon ElastiCache API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/APIReference/API_CreateGlobalReplicationGroup.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"d2a5561e-dd9f-4ec7-8176-b87961daabf6","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-cloudops-engineer-associate-soa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company operates a critical serverless application that uses multiple AWS Lambda functions. Each Lambda function produces 1 GB of log data per day in its own Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. The company’s security team requests a count of application errors, grouped by type, across all log groups."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should a CloudOps engineer do to satisfy this requirement?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Perform a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that uses the stats command and count function.","B":"Perform a CloudWatch Logs search that uses the groupby keyword and count function.","C":"Perform an Amazon Athena query that uses the SELECT and GROUP BV keywords.","D":"Perform an Amazon RDS query that uses the SELECT and GROUP BY keywords."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"CloudWatch Logs Insights can query multiple log groups and aggregate the matching log events. The `stats` command supports `count()` and grouping by a field, so it can return the count of application errors for each error type across the selected Lambda log groups.

**Learn more:** [stats - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL_QuerySyntax-Stats.html) · [Tutorial: Run a query with an aggregation function - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL_AnalyzeLogData_AggregationQuery.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"22894b24-48de-4078-a698-2b33dce9726c","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-cloudops-engineer-associate-soa-c03","mode":"default"}}]]
A CloudOps engineer is getting ready to deploy an application to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application requires installation of dependencies. Application updates are released weekly.  
  
The CloudOps engineer must implement a solution that incorporates the application updates regularly. The solution must also perform a vulnerability scan while the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is being created.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create a script that uses Packer. Schedule a cron job to run the script.
Install the application and its dependencies on an EC2 instance. Create an AMI of the EC2 instance.
Use EC2 Image Builder with a custom recipe to install the application and its dependencies.
Invoke the EC2 CreateImage API operation by using an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule.

questions.explanation:
EC2 Image Builder provides managed, repeatable AMI pipelines. A custom image recipe can install application software and dependencies, while a scheduled pipeline regularly builds updated AMIs. Image Builder also supports configuring vulnerability scans for image pipelines during image creation, so it meets the update and security requirements with less operational overhead than self-managed scripts or manually created images. [Create an AMI image pipeline from the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/cli-create-image-pipeline.html)

**Learn more:** [Create an AMI image pipeline from the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/cli-create-image-pipeline.html) · [What is EC2 Image Builder?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/what-is-image-builder.html)

A company runs compute resources in a VPC and in the company’s on-premises data center. The company already has an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC and the on-premises data center. A CloudOps engineer must ensure that Amazon EC2 instances in the VPC can resolve DNS names for hosts in the on-premises data center.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** ongoing maintenance?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone. Populate the zone with the hostnames and IP addresses of the hosts in the on-premises data center.
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Add the IP addresses of an on-premises DNS server for the domain names that need to be forwarded.
Set up a forwarding rule for reverse DNS queries in Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Set the enableDnsHostnames attribute to true for the VPC.
Add the hostnames and IP addresses for the on-premises hosts to the /etc/hosts file of each EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and forwarding rule send queries for the on-premises domain to the on-premises DNS server IP addresses over Direct Connect. The on-premises DNS infrastructure remains authoritative, avoiding per-host record maintenance in a private hosted zone or on every EC2 instance.

**Learn more:** [Forwarding outbound DNS queries to your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-outbound-queries.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global company operates a critical primary workload in the us-east-1 Region. The company wants to maintain business continuity with minimal downtime if the workload fails. The company wants to replicate the workload to a second AWS Region.  
  
A CloudOps engineer requires a solution that delivers a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 10 minutes and a zero recovery point objective (RPO) to satisfy service level agreements.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Implement a pilot light architecture that provides real-time data replication in the second Region. Configure Amazon Route 53 health checks and automated DNS failover.
Implement a warm standby architecture that provides regular data replication in a second Region. Configure Amazon Route 53 health checks and automated DNS failover.
Implement an active-active architecture that provides real-time data replication across two Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks and a weighted routing policy.

Implement a custom script to generate a regular backup of the data and store it in an S3 bucket that is in a second Region. Use the backup to launch the application in the second Region in the event of a workload failure.

questions.explanation:
A multi-site active-active architecture keeps complete, serving workload capacity in both Regions and uses real-time replication, minimizing both service interruption and data loss. AWS documents active-active as providing zero or near-zero RTO and near-zero RPO; pilot light, warm standby, and backup-and-restore have longer recovery objectives or replication gaps.

**Learn more:** [Defining your disaster recovery strategy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/strategy-database-disaster-recovery/defining.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application stores and retrieves data from an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database. A developer accidentally drops a table in the database, causing application errors. Two hours later, a CloudOps engineer must recover the data and restore application functionality.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use the Aurora Backtrack feature to rewind the database to a specified time, 2 hours in the past.
Perform a point-in-time recovery on the existing database to restore the database to a specified point in time, 2 hours in the past.
Perform a point-in-time recovery and create a new database to restore the database to a specified point in time, 2 hours in the past. Reconfigure the application to use a new database endpoint.
Create a new Aurora cluster. Choose the Restore data from S3 bucket option. Choose log files up to the failure time 2 hours in the past.

questions.explanation:
Aurora PostgreSQL supports point-in-time recovery within its backup-retention period, but that recovery creates a new DB cluster rather than restoring the existing cluster in place. Restoring the cluster to a time before the table drop and reconfiguring the application to connect to the new cluster endpoint recovers the data and allows the application to operate again. Aurora Backtrack applies to Aurora MySQL-compatible edition, not Aurora PostgreSQL.

**Learn more:** [Restoring a DB cluster to a specified time - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-pitr.html) · [Backtracking an Aurora DB cluster - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Managing.Backtrack.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application that processes events sequentially by using an Amazon SQS FIFO queue. The company needs a solution that automatically sends notifications to the SQS queue when new objects are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The solution must preserve message ordering.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that polls the objects by using the ListObjectsV2 command and detects new objects when the objects are added. Configure the Lambda function to add a message to the SQS queue when new objects are detected.
Create an event notification on the S3 bucket. Use the FIFO delivery option. Route the notifications to the existing SQS queue.
Create an Amazon SNS FIFO topic. Create an event notification on the S3 bucket. Configure the event to send messages to the SNS topic. Subscribe the existing SQS queue to the SNS topic.
Create an access point in Amazon S3 Access Points. Configure the access point to send new items to the existing SQS queue.

questions.explanation:
To preserve strict message ordering into an existing SQS FIFO queue, the notification path must itself be FIFO-aware. An SNS FIFO topic delivers messages in order and only to SQS FIFO subscribers, so routing S3 object-created events through an SNS FIFO topic that the FIFO queue subscribes to is the fully managed pattern that maintains ordering. Option B is the trap: S3 event notifications have no "FIFO delivery option" and cannot target an SQS FIFO queue directly. Option A (Lambda polling ListObjectsV2) is high operational overhead and does not guarantee ordering, and Option D misuses S3 Access Points, which do not emit events to SQS. C is the intended least-overhead ordering-preserving design.

**Learn more:** [S3 event notification destinations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html) · [SNS FIFO topics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-fifo-topics.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a business application across more than 300 Linux-based instances. AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on every instance. The company anticipates that the instance count will increase in the future. All business-application instances share the same user-defined tag.  
  
A CloudOps engineer needs to run a command on every business-application instance to download and install a package from a private repository. To prevent overloading the repository, the CloudOps engineer must ensure that no more than 30 downloads happen at the same time.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Use a secondary tag to create 10 batches of 30 instances each. Use a Systems Manager Run Command document to download and install the package. Specify the target as part of the RunCommand document by using the secondary tag. Run each batch one time.

Use an AWS Lambda function to automatically run a Systems Manager Run Command document that roads a list of instance IDs that have the user-defined tag. Set reserved concurrency for the Lambda function to 30.

Use a Systems Manager Run Command document to download and install the package. Use rate control to set concurrency to 30. Specify the target by using the user-defined tag as part of the Run Command document.

Use a parallel workflow state in AWS Step Functions to automatically run a Systems Manager Run Command document that reads a list of instance IDs that have the user-defined tag. Set the number of parallel states to 30. Run the Step Functions workflow 10 times.

questions.explanation:
Systems Manager Run Command can target a fleet of managed nodes by tag and use rate controls. Setting the Run Command concurrency (MaxConcurrency) to the absolute value 30 allows no more than 30 targeted instances to execute the command simultaneously, while tag-based targeting continues to scale as matching instances are added.

**Learn more:** [Run commands at scale - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/send-commands-multiple.html) · [SendCommand - AWS Systems Manager API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/APIReference/API_SendCommand.html)

A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver a static website hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket. The S3 bucket is the origin for the CloudFront distribution. The website has users worldwide.  
  
The company updates some website content. After the update, users report seeing the earlier version of the content.  
  
The company must make sure that website users receive only the latest content.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 ACLs to make new content public.
Reupload the new content. Set up versioning on the origin S3 bucket.
Upload new content to the same Availability Zone where the CloudFront distribution is located.
Use CloudFront invalidation when new content is uploaded.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront invalidation removes specified objects from CloudFront edge caches. On the next viewer request, CloudFront retrieves the current object from the Amazon S3 origin instead of serving the previously cached version.

**Learn more:** [Invalidate files to remove content - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Invalidation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer is building a simple public-facing website on Amazon EC2. The CloudOps engineer created the EC2 instance in an existing public subnet and assigned the instance an Elastic IP address. Next, the CloudOps engineer created and applied a new security group to the instance that permits inbound HTTP traffic from `0.0.0.0/0`. Finally, the CloudOps engineer created a new network ACL and applied it to the subnet to permit inbound HTTP traffic from `0.0.0.0/0`. However, the website cannot be accessed from the internet.  
  
What is causing this issue?

options.text: The CloudOps engineer did not create an outbound rule that allows ephemeral port return traffic in the new network ACL
The CloudOps engineer did not create an outbound rule in the security group that allows HTTP traffic from port 80.
The Elastic IP address assigned to the EC2 instance has changed.
There is an additional network ACL associated with the subnet that includes a rule that denies inbound HTTP traffic from port 80.

questions.explanation:
Network ACLs are stateless, so response traffic is not automatically allowed. An ACL that permits inbound HTTP on TCP port 80 also needs an outbound rule that permits the web server’s response traffic to the clients’ ephemeral ports. Security groups are stateful, so an inbound HTTP rule allows the corresponding response traffic without a separate outbound response rule.

**Learn more:** [Control subnet traffic with network access control lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html) · [Example: Control access to instances in a subnet](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nacl-examples.html)

A company runs an application on memory-optimized Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The company launched the EC2 instances from an AWS-provided Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Amazon Machine Image (AMI).  
  
A CloudOps engineer needs to monitor RAM utilization at 5-minute intervals. The CloudOps engineer must make sure that the EC2 instances scale in and out correctly according to incoming load.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances. Configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group and Auto Scaling policy that is based on the mem_active metric.

Configure detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances. Use the mem_used_percent metric that the detailed monitoring feature provides. Create an IAM role that allows the CloudWatch agent to upload data. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group and Auto Scaling policy that is based on the mem_used_percent metric.

Configure basic monitoring for the EC2 instances. Configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances. Create an IAM role that allows the CloudWatch agent to upload data. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group and Auto Scaling policy that is based on the mem_used_percent metric.

Configure basic monitoring for the EC2 instances. Use the standard mem_used_percent metric for monitoring. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group and Auto Scaling policy that is based on the mem_used_percent metric.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 basic monitoring supplies its built-in metrics in 5-minute periods. RAM utilization is an operating-system-level metric rather than a standard EC2 metric, so the Amazon CloudWatch agent must collect it on the RHEL instances. The agent publishes `mem_used_percent`, which is the percentage of memory currently in use, and an IAM role must authorize the agent to publish those metrics. An EC2 Auto Scaling policy can use that metric to adjust capacity.

**Learn more:** [Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/metrics-collected-by-CloudWatch-agent.html) · [Manage detailed monitoring for your EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/manage-detailed-monitoring.html)

A company assigns user-defined tags to resources associated with the company’s AWS workloads. Twenty days after applying the tags, the company finds that it cannot use them to filter views in the AWS Cost Explorer console.  
  
What is causing this issue?

options.text: It takes at least 30 days to be able to use tags to filter views in Cost Explorer.
The company has not activated the user-defined tags for cost allocation.
The company has not created an AWS Cost and Usage Report.
The company has not created a usage budget in AWS Budgets.

questions.explanation:
User-defined resource tag keys must be explicitly activated as cost allocation tags in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console before they can be used in AWS Cost Explorer. Activation normally completes within up to 24 hours, so waiting 20 days without activation does not make the tags available.

**Learn more:** [Activating user-defined cost allocation tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/activating-tags.html) · [Using user-defined cost allocation tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/custom-tags.html)
