lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s reporting job, which previously completed in 15 minutes, now takes an hour. An application produces the reports. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and retrieves data from an Amazon RDS for MySQL database.  
  
A CloudOps engineer reviews the Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for the RDS instance and observes high Read IOPS metrics, even when the reports are not running. The CloudOps engineer must improve the RDS instance’s performance and availability.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the RDS instance. Update the reporting job to query the ElastiCache cluster.
Deploy an RDS read replica. Update the reporting job to query the reader endpoint.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the RDS instance as the origin. Update the reporting job to query the CloudFront distribution.
Increase the size of the RDS instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS read replicas scale read-heavy workloads beyond the compute or I/O capacity of a single DB instance by directing read-only reporting queries away from the primary database. A read replica can be configured as a Multi-AZ DB instance to provide failover support for the replica.

**Learn more:** [Working with DB instance read replicas - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) · [Creating a read replica - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer needs to provide access to AWS services by attaching an IAM policy to multiple IAM users. The CloudOps engineer also needs to be able to modify the policy and create new versions.  
  
Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add the users to an IAM service-linked role. Attach the policy to the role.
Add the users to an IAM user group. Attach the policy to the group.
Create an AWS managed policy.
Create a customer managed policy.
Create an inline policy.

questions.explanation:
An IAM user group can grant its members the permissions from a policy attached to that group. A customer managed policy is a reusable policy managed in the account; it can be attached to groups, edited by the customer, and versioned. AWS managed policies are managed by AWS, and inline policies have a one-to-one relationship with an identity and do not support policy versioning.

**Learn more:** [Versioning IAM policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_managed-versioning.html) · [Choose between managed policies and inline policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-choosing-managed-or-inline.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has business-critical resources in an AWS account. It wants to receive an email notification whenever an AWS Management Console root-user sign-in event occurs in that account.  
  
Which solution satisfies this requirement with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that detects AWS Management Console root user sign-in events. Configure the alarm to send email notifications directly through AWS Trusted Advisor.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Schedule a script to run every hour to analyze AWS CloudTrail events. Configure the script to send email notifications to an Amazon SNS topic when AWS Management Console root user sign-in events occur.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS Management Console root user sign-in events. Configure the rule to send email notifications to an Amazon SQS queue.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS Management Console root user sign-in events. Configure the rule to send email notifications to an Amazon SNS topic.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail records root-user console sign-ins as `ConsoleLogin` events, and Amazon EventBridge rules can react to AWS Management Console sign-in events delivered through CloudTrail. An EventBridge rule can publish matching events to an Amazon SNS topic, and an email address can subscribe to that topic to receive notifications. This is a fully managed, event-driven design with no polling infrastructure to operate.

**Learn more:** [AWS Management Console sign-in events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-event-reference-aws-console-sign-in-events.html) · [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling across multiple Availability Zones and must ensure that EC2 instances are launched in private subnets.  
  
The company recently optimized its cloud infrastructure by reducing the number of NAT gateways in the company’s VPC to one. Following the infrastructure update, some EC2 instances lost internet connectivity. A CloudOps engineer must resolve the connectivity issue.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Replace the existing NAT gateway with a NAT instance in the same subnet.
Update VPC route tables to target the existing NAT gateway for internet traffic.
Update VPC route tables to target an internet gateway for internet traffic.
Add secondary IP addresses to the existing NAT gateway.

questions.explanation:
Private-subnet instances need a route-table default route for internet-bound traffic that targets a NAT gateway. Route tables that still point to NAT gateways that were removed will prevent outbound connectivity; updating them to use the remaining NAT gateway restores that connectivity.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html) · [Configure route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Route_Tables.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial services company keeps customer images in an Amazon S3 bucket in the `us-east-1` Region. To meet regulatory requirements, the company must ensure that every existing object is replicated to an S3 bucket in a second AWS Region. If replication of an object fails, the company must be able to retry that object's replication.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use Amazon S3 live replication to replicate existing objects.
Configure Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use S3 Batch Replication to replicate existing objects.
Configure Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) to replicate existing objects.
Use S3 Lifecycle rules to move objects to the destination bucket in a second Region.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication provides replication to a bucket in a different AWS Region. S3 Batch Replication is the on-demand mechanism for objects that existed before a replication configuration was created, and it can filter for objects with a `FAILED` replication status so failed replications can be retried.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Replicating existing objects with Batch Replication - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-batch-replication-batch.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer uses AWS Compute Optimizer to produce recommendations for a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. Some instances use newly released instance types, whereas others use older instance types.  
  
After the analysis finishes, the CloudOps engineer finds that some EC2 instances are absent from the Compute Optimizer dashboard.  
  
What is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The missing instances have insufficient historical Amazon CloudWatch metric data for analysis.
Compute Optimizer does not support the instance types of the missing instances.
Compute Optimizer already considers the missing instances to be optimized.
The missing instances are running a Windows operating system.

questions.explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer generates Amazon EC2 recommendations only for supported instance types. A newly released instance type can be absent until AWS adds support for it; the service does not generate recommendations for unsupported types.

**Learn more:** [Resource requirements - AWS Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/requirements.html) · [Get EC2 instance recommendations from Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-recommendations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer is troubleshooting a VPC that has public and private subnets using custom network ACLs. Instances in the private subnet cannot access the internet. An internet gateway is attached to the public subnet. The private subnet routes traffic to a NAT gateway that is also attached to the public subnet. The Amazon EC2 instances use the VPC's default security group.  
  
What is causing the issue in this scenario?

options.text: There Is a network ACL on the private subnet set to deny all outbound traffic.
There is no NAT gateway deployed in the private subnet of the VPC.
The default security group for the VPC blocks all inbound traffic to the EC2 instances.
The default security group for the VPC blocks all outbound traffic from the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
A network ACL filters traffic at the subnet level and can explicitly deny outbound traffic. Because network ACLs are stateless, a deny-all outbound rule on the private subnet prevents the instances’ internet-bound traffic from reaching the NAT gateway. A public NAT gateway belongs in a public subnet, and the default VPC security group allows all outbound IPv4 traffic.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-troubleshooting.html) · [Default security groups for your VPCs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/default-security-group.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must deploy a MySQL database on AWS to support an application. The database must be highly available and recoverable, and it must meet the following objectives:  
  
- A recovery time objective (RTO) of 15 minutes  
- A recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** operationally effective way?

options.text: Deploy a MySQL database in a single Availability Zone by using Amazon RDS. Enable automated backups.
Deploy a MySQL database across two Availability Zones by using Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment. Enable point-in-time restore.
Deploy a MySQL database across two Availability Zones by using Amazon EC2 instances. Configure database replication and Amazon EBS volume snapshots.
Deploy a MySQL database across two Availability Zones by using Amazon RDS. Enable automated backups and database replication.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment maintains a standby replica in another Availability Zone and automatically fails over during an infrastructure outage; typical failover time is 60–120 seconds, satisfying a 15-minute RTO. Amazon RDS point-in-time recovery uses automated backups and transaction logs that RDS uploads every five minutes, supporting a 5-minute RPO. Because RDS manages replication, failover, backups, and recovery, it is more operationally effective than self-managed database replication and EBS snapshots on Amazon EC2.

**Learn more:** [Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html) · [Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIT.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations to manage a collection of AWS accounts and has configured organizational units (OUs) in the organization. An application OU supports multiple applications.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must stop users from launching Amazon EC2 instances without a `CostCenter-Project` tag in any account within the application OU. The restriction must apply only to accounts in the application OU.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM group that has a policy that allows the ec2:RunInstances action when the CostCenter-Project tag is present. Place all IAM users who need access to the application accounts in the IAM group.
Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the oc2:RunInstances action when the CostCenter-Project tag is missing. Attach the SCP to the application OU.
Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows the oc2:RunInstances action when the CostCenter-Project tag is present. Attach the IAM role to the IAM users that are in the application OU accounts.
Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the ec2:RunInstances action when the CostCenter-Project tag is missing. Attach the SCP to the root OU.

questions.explanation:
An SCP attached to an OU sets a permissions boundary for all accounts in that OU. An explicit deny of `ec2:RunInstances` when `aws:RequestTag/CostCenter-Project` is absent prevents untagged EC2 instance launches even if an IAM policy otherwise allows them, while targeting only the application OU. AWS documents SCP-based tag enforcement using an explicit deny on `ec2:RunInstances` and a missing request-tag condition.

**Learn more:** [Implementing and enforcing tagging - AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/tagging-best-practices/implementing-and-enforcing-tagging.html) · [Enforce tagging consistency - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-enforcement.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer must rapidly troubleshoot problems in an application running in a production environment on Amazon EC2 instances. The application uses an Amazon RDS database. To troubleshoot these problems, the CloudOps engineer requires a centralized solution to collect and query logs from both the EC2 instances and the RDS database.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to forward ERROR log events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure the RDS database to export log events to CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query the logs.

Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to forward INFO log events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Install the CloudWatch agent on the RDS database. Forward ERROR log events to the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke AWS Lambda functions to analyze the logs.

Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to forward ERROR log events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use the Logs & events menu to examine log events for the RDS database. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query logs only for the EC2 instances.

Install and configure the AWS X-Ray agent on the EC2 instances to forward INFO, DEBUG, and latency log events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure the RDS database to export log events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query the logs.

questions.explanation:
The CloudWatch agent collects application logs from Amazon EC2 instances and sends them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Amazon RDS can export supported database logs directly to CloudWatch Logs, where CloudWatch Logs Insights can interactively search and analyze the centralized log data across the selected log groups.

**Learn more:** [Collect metrics, logs, and traces using the CloudWatch agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html) · [Publishing database logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_LogAccess.Procedural.UploadtoCloudWatch.html)

options.text: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to perform a check for S3 buckets that do not have logging enabled. Configure the check to enable logging for S3 buckets that do not have logging enabled.
Configure an S3 bucket policy that requires all current and future S3 buckets to have logging enabled.
Use the s3-bucket-logging-enabled AWS Config managed rule. Add a remediation action that uses an AWS Lambda function to enable logging.
Use the s3-bucket-logging-enabled AWS Config managed rule. Add a remediation action that uses the AWS-ConfigureS3BucketLogging AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to enable logging.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Config `s3-bucket-logging-enabled` managed rule checks S3 buckets and reports a bucket as NON_COMPLIANT when logging is not enabled. A remediation action that invokes the `AWS-ConfigureS3BucketLogging` AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook can automatically enable S3 server access logging, covering both existing buckets and buckets evaluated after future configuration changes.

**Learn more:** [s3-bucket-logging-enabled - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-logging-enabled.html) · [AWS-ConfigureS3BucketLogging - AWS Systems Manager Automation Runbook Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-aws-configures3bucketlogging.html)

An Amazon EC2 instance runs an application that uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. A CloudOps engineer must make sure the application can read, write, and delete messages in the SQS queues.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** secure way?

options.text: Create an IAM user with an IAM policy that allows the sqs:SendMessage permission, the sqsReceiveMessage permission, and the sqs:DeleteMessage permission to the appropriate queues. Embed the IAM user's credentials in the application’s configuration.

Create an IAM user with an IAM policy that allows the sqs:SendMessage permission, the sqs:ReceiveMessage permission, and the sqs:DeleteMessage permission to the appropriate queues. Export the IAM user's access key and secret access key as environment variables on the EC2 instance.
Create and associate an IAM role that allows EC2 instances to call AWS services. Attach an IAM policy to the role that allows sqs:* permissions to the appropriate queues.

Create and associate an IAM role that allows EC2 instances to call AWS services. Attach an IAM policy to the role that allows the sqs:SendMessage permission, the sqs:ReceiveMessage permission, and the sqs:DeleteMessage permission to the appropriate queues.

questions.explanation:
An IAM role associated with the EC2 instance supplies temporary credentials to the application without distributing long-term IAM user access keys. Limiting the role policy to `sqs:SendMessage`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, and `sqs:DeleteMessage` on the appropriate queues follows least privilege, whereas `sqs:*` grants unnecessary permissions.

**Learn more:** [Use an IAM role to grant permissions to applications running on Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_switch-role-ec2.html) · [IAM roles for Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/iam-roles-for-amazon-ec2.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations to manage a group of AWS accounts. The company’s security team wants to use a native AWS service to regularly assess all AWS accounts against the Center for Internet Security (CIS) AWS Foundations Benchmark.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient way to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Designate a central security account as the AWS Security Hub administrator account. Create a script that sends an invitation from the Security Hub administrator account and accepts the invitation from the member account. Run the script every time a new account is created. Configure Security Hub to run the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark scans.
Run the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark across all accounts by using Amazon Inspector.

Designate a central security account as the Amazon GuardDuty administrator account. Create a script that sends an invitation from the GuardDuty administrator account and accepts the invitation from the member account. Run the script every time a new account is created. Configure GuardDuty to run the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark scans.
Designate an AWS Security Hub administrator account. Configure new accounts in the organization to automatically become member accounts. Enable CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark scans.

questions.explanation:
AWS Security Hub CSPM supports the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark and integrates with AWS Organizations. A Security Hub administrator can configure organization accounts so that new accounts automatically become member accounts, enabling centralized, ongoing CIS security-standard findings without scripts or per-account invitations.

**Learn more:** [Automatically enabling Security Hub CSPM in new organization accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/accounts-orgs-auto-enable.html) · [CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark in Security Hub CSPM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a custom Amazon Machine Image (AMI) in an EC2 Image Builder pipeline. A CloudOps engineer discovers that the custom AMI will reach the end of its support lifespan in a few months. The CloudOps engineer must update the EC2 Image Builder pipeline to use the most recent AMI ID.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Create a new version of the existing EC2 Image Builder recipe. Update the AMI ID details. Update the pipeline to use the new recipe version.
Disable the AMI in the lifecycle rules for the existing AMI. Update the existing EC2 Image Builder recipe with the latest AMI ID details. Rerun the pipeline.
Update the build component to use the latest AMI ID details.
Replace the AMI ID in the launch template for the pipeline.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 Image Builder image recipe specifies the parent AMI used as the base image, and recipes cannot be modified after they are created. To change the base AMI ID, create a new version of the recipe with the updated parent image and update the pipeline to use that recipe version.

**Learn more:** [Update AMI image pipelines from the console - EC2 Image Builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/update-image-pipeline-console.html) · [Manage recipes in EC2 Image Builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/imagebuilder/latest/userguide/manage-recipes.html)

A company operates a workload in an Amazon VPC and configures Amazon CloudWatch Logs for that workload. The company requires a solution that automatically detects unusual API activity and security events in the company’s AWS account.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon Inspector to scan VPC flow logs.
Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor CloudWatch logs.
Implement AWS CloudTrail Insights.
Use AWS Config automatic anomaly detection.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail Insights continuously analyzes CloudTrail management and data events to establish normal API call and error-rate baselines, then generates Insights events when API activity deviates from those baselines. This provides automatic detection of unusual account API activity relevant to security monitoring.\
\
**Learn more:** [Working with CloudTrail Insights](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-insights-events-with-cloudtrail.html)

questions.question:
A company operates a microservice on a group of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are positioned behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
A CloudOps engineer must use Amazon Route 53 to create a record that maps the ALB URL to example.com.  
  
Which record type meets this requirement?

options.text: An A record
An AAAA record
An alias record
A CNAME record

questions.explanation:
An Amazon Route 53 alias record can point to an Elastic Load Balancing Application Load Balancer and lets the zone-apex domain `example.com` resolve to the load balancer. Route 53 automatically follows changes to the load balancer’s underlying IP addresses; a CNAME record cannot be created at the zone apex.\
\
**Learn more:** [Choosing between alias and non-alias records - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resource-record-sets-choosing-alias-non-alias.html)

questions.question:
A company operates a microservice on a group of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are positioned behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
A CloudOps engineer must use Amazon Route 53 to create a record that maps the ALB URL to example.com.  
  
Which record type meets this requirement?

options.text: Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke the EC2 instance when images are uploaded to the S3 bucket. Run the image processing solution on the EC2 instance to process the images.
Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an Amazon EventBridge rule. Configure the EventBridge rule to start a preconfigured AWS Glue ETL job to process images.
Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function that runs image processing logic when new images are uploaded on the source S3 bucket.

Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke a task on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container that is backed by EC2 instances when the images are uploaded to the S3 bucket. Configure the ECS task to process the images.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 can invoke an AWS Lambda function for object-created events, and Lambda runs custom code only in response to those events. A 30–120 second processing duration is suitable for Lambda, so the direct event-driven design eliminates the need to keep EC2 capacity running continuously.

**Learn more:** [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html) · [Event notification types and destinations - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html)

questions.question:
A company is working to manage its costs in the AWS Cloud. A CloudOps engineer needs specific company-defined tags assigned to resources to be displayed on the billing report.  
  
What should the CloudOps engineer do to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Activate the tags as AWS generated cost allocation tags.
Activate the tags as user-defined cost allocation tags.
Create a new cost category. Select the account billing dimension.
Create a new AWS Cost and Usage Report. Include the resource IDs.

questions.explanation:
Company-defined resource tags are user-defined cost allocation tags. Activating those tag keys in AWS Billing and Cost Management makes them available in cost allocation and billing reports; AWS-generated tags are created by AWS, not by the company.\
\
**Learn more:** [Activating user-defined cost allocation tags - AWS Billing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/activating-tags.html)

questions.question:
A CloudOps engineer configured AWS Backup to take snapshots of a single Amazon EC2 instance with one attached Amazon EBS volume. At the time of the first snapshot, the EBS volume contains 10 GiB of data. At the time of the second snapshot, the EBS volume still contains 10 GiB of data, but 4 GiB has changed. At the time of the third snapshot, 2 GiB of data has been added to the volume, bringing the total to 12 GiB.  
  
How much total storage is needed to store these snapshots?

options.text: 12 GIB
16 GiB
26 GiB
32 GIB

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS snapshots are incremental: the first snapshot stores the initial 10 GiB, while later snapshots store only blocks changed since the preceding snapshot. The storage required is therefore 10 GiB + 4 GiB + 2 GiB = 16 GiB.\
\
**Learn more:** [How Amazon EBS snapshots work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/how_snapshots_work.html)

questions.question:

At the time of the third snapshot, 2 GiB of data has been added to the volume, bringing the total to 12 GiB.  
  
How much total storage is needed to store these snapshots?

options.text: In all member accounts, configure IAM policies that deny access to all DynamoDB resources for all users, including the root user.
Create a service control policy (SCP) in the management account to deny all DynamoDB actions. Apply the SCP to the root of the organization.
In all member accounts, configure IAM policies that deny AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess to all users, including the root user.
Remove the default service control policy (SCP) in the management account. Create a replacement SCP that includes a single statement that denies all DynamoDB actions.

questions.explanation:
A service control policy attached to the organization root applies to every member account, including each member account’s root user. An explicit deny of all DynamoDB actions overrides otherwise granted permissions, while the default FullAWSAccess SCP continues to allow other AWS services subject to their IAM permissions.

**Learn more:** [Service control policies (SCPs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html) · [SCP evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s CloudOps engineer is troubleshooting communication among the components of an application. The company configured VPC Flow Logs to publish to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, but no logs appear in CloudWatch Logs.  
  
What could prevent the VPC Flow Logs from being published to CloudWatch Logs?

options.text: The IAM policy that is attached to the IAM role for the flow log is missing the logs:CreateLogGroup permission.
The IAM policy that is attached to the IAM role for the flow log is missing the logs:CreateExportTask permission.
The VPC is configured for IPv6 addresses.
The VPC is peered with another VPC in the AWS account

questions.explanation:
The IAM role used by a VPC flow log needs CloudWatch Logs delivery permissions, including `logs:CreateLogGroup`. If that permission is absent, the service can be unable to create the destination log group and publish flow-log records. `logs:CreateExportTask` is unrelated to flow-log delivery, and neither IPv6 nor VPC peering inherently blocks publication to CloudWatch Logs.

**Learn more:** [IAM role for publishing flow logs to CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-iam-role.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to host an application on Amazon EC2 instances distributed across multiple Availability Zones. The application must scale to millions of requests per second.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must design a solution that distributes traffic to the EC2 instances. The solution must be optimized for sudden, volatile traffic patterns while using a single static IP address for each Availability Zone.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue
Application Load Balancer
AWS Global Accelerator
Network Load Balancer

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer can handle volatile workloads and scale to millions of requests per second. It distributes traffic to registered EC2 targets in enabled Availability Zones and provides one static IP address per enabled Availability Zone; an Elastic IP address can be assigned for each subnet/Availability Zone. [AWS Network Load Balancer documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html)

**Learn more:** [What is a Network Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's developers deploy applications across multiple AWS accounts. The developers can create any AWS resource within those AWS accounts.  
  
A security team needs to audit the resources that the developers create in the company's AWS accounts.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Create an AWS account for the security team. Configure AWS Audit Manager in the security team's account. Create an Audit Manager assessment. Include the company's AWS accounts in the assessment scope. Generate an assessment report for the security team.

Configure an AWS Config recorder in each AWS account. In the security team's AWS account, create an AWS Config aggregator. Authorize the aggregator in every AWS account. Use Amazon Quick Suite and Amazon Athena to generate a report for the security team.

Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail in every AWS account. Create an Amazon RDS DB instance in the security team's account. Configure CloudTrail in every account to write logs to the DB instance. Use Amazon Quick Suite to query the DB instance and generate a report for the security team.

Enable AWS Trusted Advisor in every AWS account. Create a scheduled Amazon EventBridge rule to periodically refresh the Trusted Advisor checks. Use the Trusted Advisor console to generate a report for the security team.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config configuration recorders capture AWS resource configuration and inventory data. An AWS Config aggregator in the security team's account can collect configuration and compliance data from multiple authorized AWS accounts, providing a centralized, read-only view of the resources across those accounts.

**Learn more:** [What Is AWS Config?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/WhatIsConfig.html) · [Multi-Account Multi-Region Data Aggregation for AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/aggregate-data.html)

A company operates a web application on three Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company observes that random intervals of increased traffic degrade the application's performance. A CloudOps engineer must scale the application to handle the increased traffic.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor application latency and increase the size of each EC2 instance if the desired threshold is reached.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to monitor application latency and add an EC2 instance to the ALB if the desired threshold is reached.
Deploy the application to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances with a target tracking scaling policy. Attach the ALB to the Auto Scaling group.
Deploy the application to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances with a scheduled scaling policy. Attach the ALB to the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
A target tracking policy dynamically changes an EC2 Auto Scaling group's capacity to maintain a specified utilization or throughput target, including Application Load Balancer request count per target. Attaching the ALB to the Auto Scaling group lets newly launched instances receive traffic, making this suitable for unpredictable demand increases. Scheduled scaling is for anticipated, time-based demand patterns.

**Learn more:** [Target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-target-tracking.html) · [Create a target tracking scaling policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/policy_creating.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company engages a cybersecurity company to audit the ecommerce company’s AWS account. The cybersecurity company asks for read-only access to that account. The ecommerce company creates an IAM role, adds a trust relationship with the cybersecurity company’s AWS account, and adds read-only permissions to the ecommerce company’s account.  
  
An employee of the cybersecurity company unsuccessfully attempts to assume the read-only role created by the ecommerce company.  
  
A CloudOps engineer at the ecommerce company must fix the access issue.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA).
Configure an identity provider by using OpenID Connect (OIDC).
Create a policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole action. Add the policy to the cybersecurity employee's role. Ensure that the resource for the policy is the role that the employee needs to assume.
Create a policy that allows the sts:SetSourceIdentity action. Add the policy to the cybersecurity employee's role. Ensure that the resource for the policy is in the ecommerce company's account.

questions.explanation:
For cross-account role access, the target role’s trust policy must trust the external account or principal, and the calling identity in that external account must also have an identity-based policy allowing `sts:AssumeRole` on the target role’s ARN. Granting that permission to the cybersecurity employee’s role enables it to assume the ecommerce company’s read-only role.

**Learn more:** [Update a role trust policy - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_update-role-trust-policy.html) · [Cross-account policy evaluation logic - AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic-cross-account.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer needs to configure observability for specific metrics for a public website running on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The CloudOps engineer needs to observe latency, traffic, errors, and saturation metrics. The CloudOps engineer needs to define service level objectives (SLOs) and monitor service level indicators (SLIs). The CloudOps engineer also needs to correlate metrics, logs, and traces to enable faster issue resolution.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals to automatically collect and monitor the specified metrics for the EKS workloads.

Configure AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry for the website to generate metrics. Use Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus to collect the specified metrics. Use Amazon Managed Grafana to visualize metrics.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch RUM and CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to automatically collect and monitor the specified metrics for the EKS workloads.
Configure Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights to detect common application performance problems and anomalies and to monitor the specified metrics for the EKS workloads.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch Application Signals provides managed application performance monitoring for Amazon EKS workloads. It automatically collects application metrics and traces, provides latency, traffic, fault/error, and runtime metrics for service health and saturation analysis, supports creating and tracking SLOs and SLIs, and supplies correlated application telemetry and topology views for faster troubleshooting.

**Learn more:** [Application Signals - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Application-Monitoring-Sections.html) · [Service level objectives (SLOs) - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-ServiceLevelObjectives.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A developer uses an Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to launch an EC2 instance that hosts a third-party application. The application periodically becomes unstable. The CloudOps engineer needs a solution that automatically reboots the EC2 instance whenever utilization exceeds 90% for 15 minutes and notifies the developer about the reboot.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative effort?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that evaluates the CPU utilization of the instance. Configure the alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the CloudWatch alarm activates. Configure the Lambda function to reboot the EC2 instance. Subscribe the developer to the SNS topic.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that evaluates the CPU utilization of the instance. Configure the alarm to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and to perform an EC2 action to reboot the instance. Subscribe the developer to the SNS topic.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that evaluates the CPU utilization of the instance Configure the alarm to invoke an AWS Systems Manager action to create an incident to notify the developer and request the reboot.

Create an AWS Systems Manager runbook script to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and to reboot the EC2 instance. Subscribe the developer to the SNS topic. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to run the Systems Manager runbook when CPU utilization for the instance remains above 90% for more than 15 minutes.

questions.explanation:
CloudWatch alarms based on an EC2 per-instance metric can directly perform EC2 actions, including rebooting the instance, and can simultaneously publish a notification to an SNS topic. Configuring the alarm for CPU utilization above 90% for 15 minutes, adding the reboot action, and subscribing the developer to the SNS topic satisfies both requirements without custom Lambda code or Systems Manager automation.

**Learn more:** [Stop, terminate, reboot, or recover an EC2 instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/UsingAlarmActions.html) · [Alarm actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/alarm-actions.html)

A company intends to deploy a database on an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The database will hold data for a demonstration environment, and that data must be reset each day.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create a manual snapshot of the DB cluster after the data has been populated. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a daily basis. Configure the function to restore the snapshot and then delete the previous DB cluster.

Enable the Backtrack feature during the creation of the DB cluster. Specify a target backtrack window of 48 hours. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a daily basis. Configure the function to perform a backtrack operation.

Export a manual snapshot of the DB cluster to an Amazon S3 bucket after the data has been populated. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a daily basis. Configure the function to restore the snapshot from Amazon S3.

Set the DB cluster backup retention period to 2 days. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function on a daily basis. Configure the function to restore the DB cluster to a point in time and then delete the previous DB cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora MySQL Backtrack rewinds an existing DB cluster to a specified time without restoring from a backup or replacing the cluster. A 48-hour target backtrack window supports a daily scheduled reset, so an EventBridge-triggered Lambda can perform the backtrack with less operational overhead than snapshot or point-in-time restore workflows.

**Learn more:** [Backtracking an Aurora DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Managing.Backtrack.html) · [Performing a backtrack for an Aurora MySQL DB cluster](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Managing.Backtrack.Performing0.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application on an Amazon EC2 instance. The web server logs are sent to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The log events share the same structure and include the HTTP response codes associated with user requests. The company must monitor how many times the web server returns an HTTP 404 response.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter that counts the number of times that the web server returns an HTTP 404 response.
Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter that counts the number of times that the web server returns an HTTP 404 response.
Create an AWS Lambda function that runs a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that counts the number of 404 codes in the log events during the past hour.
Create a script that runs a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that counts the number of 404 codes in the log events during the past hour.

questions.explanation:
A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can match log events containing an HTTP 404 response and publish a metric value of 1 for every match, producing the required count automatically as logs are ingested. This avoids custom code, scheduled queries, and separate processing infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Creating metrics from log events using filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html) · [Create a metric filter for a log group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CreateMetricFilterProcedure.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 Windows instances in a Multi-AZ deployment. The company requires a solution that provides the instances with access to shared files.  
  
The solution must be highly available, use native Windows storage capabilities, and maximize consistency for every file request.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system. Map file shares on the instances by using the file system's DNS name.
Grant the instances access to a shared Amazon S3 bucket. Use Windows Task Scheduler to synchronize the contents of the S3 bucket locally to each instance periodically.
Create an Amazon EFS file system that uses the EFS Standard storage class. Mount the file system to the instances by using the file system's DNS name and the EFS mount helper.
Create a new Amazon EBS Multi-Attach volume. Attach the EBS volume as an additional drive to each instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ provides managed SMB file shares with native Windows file-system features. It maintains a standby file server in a separate Availability Zone, replicates data synchronously, and automatically fails over while retaining the file system DNS name, providing highly available and consistent shared access for Windows instances.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html) · [Availability and durability: Single-AZ and Multi-AZ file systems](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company asks a CloudOps engineer to provision an additional application environment in four more AWS Regions. The application runs on more than 100 Amazon EC2 instances in the `us-east-1` Region and uses fully configured Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). The company has an AWS CloudFormation template that deploys resources in `us-east-1`.  
  
What should the CloudOps engineer do to provision the application in the **MOST** operationally efficient way?

options.text: Copy the AMI to each Region by using the aws ec2 copy-image command. Update the CloudFormation template to include mappings for the copied AMIs.
Create a snapshot of the running instance. Copy the snapshot to the other Regions. Create an AMI from the snapshots. Update the CloudFormation template for each Region to use the new AMI.
Run the existing CloudFormation template in each additional Region based on the success of the template that is used currently in us-east-1.
Update the CloudFormation template to include the additional Regions in the Auto Scaling group. Update the existing stack in us-east-1.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 AMIs are Region-specific, so a fully configured AMI must be copied to each destination Region before instances can be launched there. Each copied AMI receives a distinct AMI ID; a CloudFormation Region-to-AMI mapping lets one template choose the correct destination-Region image. This avoids the unnecessary snapshot-and-recreate process and is required because an Auto Scaling group and an AMI cannot directly span AWS Regions.

**Learn more:** [Copy an Amazon EC2 AMI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/CopyingAMIs.html) · [CloudFormation template Mappings syntax](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/mappings-section-structure.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
A CloudOps engineer must implement deployments with no service interruption. The company requires the ability to shift traffic between application versions and rapidly revert to the prior version by redirecting traffic if problems occur.  
  
Which deployment approach meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment with two ALB target groups. Deploy the new version to a separate fleet. Shift traffic gradually to the new target group. Maintain the original fleet for immediate rollback if necessary.

Implement an in-place rolling update by using Auto Scaling instance refresh on the existing target group. Configure connection draining for each instance. Update the launch template. Rely on health checks during the replacement process.

Create a new AMI by using the updated application. Modify the Auto Scaling launch template. Temporarily increase desired capacity to add new instances. Then terminate old instances while using ALB connection draining to manage the transition.

Design an AWS Step Functions workflow that creates a parallel Auto Scaling group and updates monitoring configurations. Configure the workflow to change instance registrations on the ALB and automatically terminate the previous fleet after a verification period.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployments provision a separate replacement environment and use Elastic Load Balancing target groups to reroute application traffic to that environment. The original environment can be kept running after traffic is shifted, allowing traffic to be redirected back to the prior application version for a rapid rollback.

**Learn more:** [Create a deployment group for an EC2/On-Premises blue/green deployment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-groups-create-blue-green.html) · [Integrating CodeDeploy with Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/integrations-aws-elastic-load-balancing.html)

questions.domain: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an ecommerce website on a fleet of Nitro-based Amazon EC2 Linux instances. During a recent sales event, some customers experienced HTTP timeout errors.  
  
To help determine the root cause of the errors, a CloudOps engineer requires more detailed network metrics from the Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) driver. The CloudOps engineer must obtain the `conntrack_allowance_available` metric and the `conntrack_allowance_exceeded` metric.  
  
Which solution will provide these metrics with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the instances. Filter by the conntrack_allowance_available metric and the conntrack_allowance_exceeded metric.
Install the collectd daemon and the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances. Filter by the conntrack_allowance_available metric and the conntrack_allowance_exceeded metric.
Enable VPC Flow Logs. Filter by the conntrack_allowance_available metric and the conntrack_allowance_exceeded metric.
Enable Performance Insights for the instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch to view the conntrack_allowance_available metric and the conntrack_allowance_exceeded metric.

questions.explanation:
The Amazon CloudWatch agent can collect ENA driver network-performance metrics when the required metrics are configured in its `ethtool` metrics collection section. This directly supports `conntrack_allowance_available` and `conntrack_allowance_exceeded` without deploying the additional collectd daemon. The available-allowance metric requires ENA driver version 2.8.1 or later on Nitro-based Linux instances.

**Learn more:** [Monitor network performance for ENA settings on your EC2 instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-network-performance-ena.html) · [Collect network performance metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Agent-network-performance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has numerous accounts in an AWS Organizations organization. The company needs to automate resource provisioning from the organization’s management account to its member accounts.  
  
Which solution fulfills this requirement?

options.text: Create an AWS CloudFormation change set. Deploy the change set to all member accounts.
Create an AWS CloudFormation nested stack. Deploy the nested stack to all member accounts.
Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set. Deploy the stack set to all member accounts.
Create an AWS SAM template. Deploy the template to all member accounts.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation StackSets deploy and manage stack instances across multiple AWS accounts. Using service-managed permissions with AWS Organizations allows the organization’s management account to target member accounts or organizational units for centralized provisioning.

**Learn more:** [AWS CLI create-stack-set reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudformation/create-stack-set.html)

questions.domain: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates several workloads on AWS. It identifies five AWS Trusted Advisor service quota metrics to monitor in a particular AWS Region. The company wants to receive an email notification whenever resource usage exceeds 60% of any service quota.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create five Amazon CloudWatch alarms, one for each Trusted Advisor service quota metric. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for email notification each time that usage exceeds 60% of one of the service quotas.

Create five Amazon CloudWatch alarms, one for each Trusted Advisor service quota metric. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for email notification each time that usage exceeds 60% of one of the service quotas.

Use the AWS Health Dashboard to monitor each Trusted Advisor service quota metric. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for email notification each time that usage exceeds 60% of one of the service quotas.

Use the AWS Health Dashboard to monitor each Trusted Advisor service quota metric. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for email notification each time that usage exceeds 60% of one of the service quotas.

questions.explanation:
AWS Trusted Advisor publishes the `ServiceLimitUsage` percentage metric for service quotas to Amazon CloudWatch. A CloudWatch alarm can monitor each quota metric at a 60% threshold and, on entering the ALARM state, notify an Amazon SNS topic. An SNS topic can have an email subscription, enabling email delivery for each alarm notification.

**Learn more:** [Creating Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor AWS Trusted Advisor metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cloudwatch-metrics-ta.html) · [Visualizing your service quotas and setting alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Quotas-Visualize-Alarms.html)

options.text: Replace ElastiCache (Redis OSS) with ElastiCache (Memcached).
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate a backup every hour. Restore the backup when necessary.
Create a read replica in a second Availability Zone. Enable Multi-AZ for the ElastiCache (Redis OSS) replication group.
Enable automatic backups. Restore the backups when necessary.

questions.explanation:
An ElastiCache Redis OSS replication group with a read replica in another Availability Zone and Multi-AZ enabled provides automatic failover if the primary node or its Availability Zone fails. ElastiCache promotes a replica to primary, typically allowing writes to resume within seconds, which improves resilience and minimizes RTO. [Minimizing downtime in ElastiCache by using Multi-AZ with Valkey and Redis OSS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html)

A company hosts a public website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company requires the website to support HTTPS connections.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue a public SSL/TLS certificate. Configure the ALB to use the certificate.
Import a public SSL/TLS certificate into AWS KMS. Configure the ALB to retrieve the certificate from AWS KMS.
Attach a public SSL/TLS certificate to the target group that is associated with the ALB.

questions.explanation:
An ALB HTTPS listener requires an SSL/TLS server certificate. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) can issue a public certificate and deploy it to the ALB, allowing the load balancer to terminate HTTPS connections before forwarding requests to the EC2 targets.

**Learn more:** [Create an HTTPS listener for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/create-https-listener.html) · [SSL certificates for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/https-listener-certificates.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is completing an external audit of systems that run entirely on AWS. A CloudOps engineer must provide documentation demonstrating Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) compliance for the infrastructure that AWS manages.  
  
Which actions should the CloudOps engineer take to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Download the applicable reports from the AWS Artifact portal and supply these to the auditors.
Download complete copies of the AWS CloudTrail log files and supply these to the auditors.
Download complete copies of the Amazon CloudWatch logs and supply these to the auditors.
Provide the auditors with administrative access to the production AWS account so that the auditors can determine compliance.

questions.explanation:
AWS Artifact provides on-demand AWS security and compliance documents, including PCI reports, and AWS states that these documents can be submitted to auditors or regulators as audit artifacts. These reports document AWS-managed controls under the shared responsibility model; operational logs do not replace them, and auditors do not need production administrative access to obtain AWS compliance documentation.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Artifact?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/artifact/latest/ug/what-is-aws-artifact.html) · [Downloading reports in AWS Artifact](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/artifact/latest/ug/downloading-documents.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s application is running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company configured an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor the `HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count` metric. The application crashes every few days during business hours. These crashes trigger the CloudWatch alarm and cause service disruption.  
  
A memory leak in the application is causing the crashes. While developers work to resolve the issue, a CloudOps engineer must implement a temporary solution. The solution must automatically reboot the EC2 instances each day and minimize application disruption during business hours.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is scheduled to run outside of business hours. Configure the rule to invoke the StartInstances operation on the EC2 instances.

Use AWS Systems Manager to create a daily maintenance window that is outside of business hours. Register the EC2 instances as a target. Assign the AWS-RestartEC2Instance runbook to the maintenance window.
Configure an additional CloudWatch alarm to monitor the StatusCheckFailed_System metric for the EC2 instances. Configure an EC2 action on the additional alarm to reboot the instances.
Configure an additional CloudWatch alarm that is triggered every time the application crashes. Configure an EC2 action on the additional alarm to restart the application on the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows schedules potentially disruptive operations during defined maintenance periods. Registering the EC2 instances as targets and assigning the `AWS-RestartEC2Instance` Automation runbook performs a daily restart at an off-hours time. The runbook restarts one or more EC2 instances, satisfying the required reboot operation.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/maintenance-windows.html) · [AWS-RestartEC2Instance Automation Runbook Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager-automation-runbooks/latest/userguide/automation-aws-restartec2instance.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company manages a globally used website hosted on Amazon EC2 behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). To decrease load on the web servers, a CloudOps engineer configures an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the ALB as its origin. After monitoring the solution for a week, the CloudOps engineer observes that requests are still served by the ALB and that web server load has not changed.  
  
What could be causing this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: CloudFront does not have the ALB configured as the origin access identity.
The DNS is still pointing to the ALB instead of the CloudFront distribution.
The ALB security group is not permitting inbound traffic from CloudFront.
The default, minimum, and maximum Time to Live (TTL) are set to 0 seconds on the CloudFront distribution.
The target groups associated with the ALB are configured for sticky sessions.

questions.explanation:
DNS must route the website’s domain name to the CloudFront distribution; if it still points to the ALB, viewers bypass CloudFront and reach the ALB directly. In addition, CloudFront caching is disabled when the minimum, default, and maximum TTL settings are all 0 seconds, causing requests to be forwarded to the origin instead of being served from the edge cache.

**Learn more:** [Distribution settings - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesGeneral.html) · [Understand cache policies - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cache-key-understand-cache-policy.html)

A CloudOps engineer must create an event infrastructure for a collection of custom, application-specific events. The events must be delivered to an AWS Lambda function for processing. The CloudOps engineer must retain the events so they can be replayed later by event type or event time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus. Create an archive on the custom event bus. Create a rule to send the custom events to the Lambda function.
Create an archive on the Amazon EventBridge default event bus. Use pattern matching to record the custom events. Create a rule to send the custom events to the Lambda function.

Create an archive on the Amazon EventBridge default event bus. Create an EventBridge pipe to ingest the custom events and to save the custom events in the archive. Create a rule to send the custom events to the Lambda function.
Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to send the custom events to the Lambda function and to the log group.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon EventBridge custom event bus provides a dedicated bus for application-specific events. An archive on that bus stores the events and can use an event pattern to retain selected event types; EventBridge replays archived events for a specified event-time range. A rule on the custom event bus can route matching events to the AWS Lambda function.

**Learn more:** [Creating event buses in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-event-bus.html) · [Creating event archives in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-archive-event.html)

A company operates a three-tier web application on AWS. The application consists of web servers, application servers, and database servers. The application servers handle requests from the web servers.  
  
The company wants to provide high availability for the application. It therefore must monitor the health of the application servers and send traffic only to healthy instances.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the application servers with health checks for the application servers.
Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for the application servers. Attach a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the application servers.

Create an AWS Lambda function that restarts an application server. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor the health of the application servers. Run the function when an application is unhealthy.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric to monitor the health of the application servers. Route traffic by using a Network Load Balancer (NLB).

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer uses target-group health checks to assess registered application-server instances and routes requests only to healthy targets. This provides health-aware traffic distribution for the application tier.

**Learn more:** [Health checks for Application Load Balancer target groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/target-group-health-checks.html) · [Application Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company gathers operating-system logs in an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. The company needs a solution that automatically alerts a support team when a particular exception occurs in the logs more than 5 times during 10 minutes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a metric filter in the log group. Create an alarm based on the metric with a period of 10 minutes. Create an Amazon SNS topic. Point the alarm to the SNS topic. Subscribe the support team's email address to the SNS topic.
Create a CloudWatch dashboard. Add a table widget to the dashboard. Populate the table with data from CloudWatch Logs Insights. Share the dashboard with the support team.

Create an AWS Lambda subscription filter to send all logs that match the search pattern to a Lambda function. Create an Amazon SNS topic to receive notifications from the Lambda function. Subscribe the support team's email address to the SNS topic.
Give the support team read-only access to the CloudWatch Logs log group so that the team can review the logs autonomously.

questions.explanation:
A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can match the exception and increment a CloudWatch metric for each matching log event. A CloudWatch alarm can evaluate that metric over a 10-minute period and, when the count exceeds 5, invoke an Amazon SNS topic action that delivers an email notification to the support team.

**Learn more:** [Creating metrics from log events using filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html) · [Alarming on logs - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Alarm-On-Logs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating a legacy application to AWS. The company manually installs and configures the legacy application on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. The company configures an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the application and sets the target group's routing algorithm to weighted random. The application requires session affinity.  
  
After deploying the application, users report intermittent application errors that did not occur in the legacy version. Target group health checks show no failures. The company must resolve the application errors.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Set the routing algorithm of the target group to least outstanding requests.
Turn on anomaly mitigation for the target group.
Turn off the cross-zone load balancing attribute of the target group.
Increase the deregistration delay attribute of the target group.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer weighted random routing cannot be used with sticky sessions, which provide session affinity. Changing the target group to least outstanding requests permits sticky sessions so subsequent requests in a user session can be routed to the same target. [AWS: Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

**Learn more:** [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application that gathers notifications from thousands of alarm systems. The notifications consist of alarm notifications and information notifications. Information notifications include system arming processes, disarming processes, and sensor status.  
  
All notifications are retained as messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group process the messages. A CloudOps engineer must implement a solution that gives alarm notifications priority over information notifications.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Adjust the Auto Scaling group to scale faster when a high number of messages is in the queue.
Use the Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) fanout feature with Amazon SQS to send the notifications in parallel to all the EC2 instances.
Add an Amazon DynamoDB stream to accelerate the message processing.
Create a queue for alarm notifications and a queue for information notifications. Update the application to collect messages from the alarm notifications queue first.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS has no built-in per-message priority capability. Separate queues enable consumers to poll and process alarm notifications before information notifications, providing the required priority while retaining both message types for processing.

**Learn more:** [How to Automatically Prevent Email Throttling when Reaching Concurrency Limit](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/messaging-and-targeting/prevent-email-throttling-concurrency-limit/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances from custom Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) across two AWS Regions. The company has registered every instance with AWS Systems Manager.  
  
The company discovers a significant zero-day exploit in the operating system on some instances, but does not know how many instances are affected.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must implement a solution to deploy operating-system patches to the affected EC2 instances.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Define a patch baseline in Systems Manager Patch Manager. Use a Patch Manager scan to identify the affected instances. Use the Patch Now option in each Region to update the affected instances.
Use AWS Config to identify the affected instances. Define a patch baseline in Systems Manager Patch Manager. Use the Patch Now option in Patch Manager to update the affected instances.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to react to Systems Manager Compliance events. Configure the EventBridge rule to run a patch baseline on the affected instances.
Use AWS Config to identify the affected instances. Update the existing EC2 AMIs with the desired patch Manually launch instances from the new AMIs to replace the affected instances in both Regions.

questions.explanation:
Systems Manager Patch Manager uses a patch baseline to define approved patches. A Patch Manager Scan identifies managed nodes that are missing those patches and reports their patch-compliance status. Patch Now can then run a Scan and install operation for the affected managed nodes. Performing the on-demand workflow in each Region directly handles the regional EC2 fleets with minimal additional infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager.html) · [Patching managed nodes on demand](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-patch-now-on-demand.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a web application that experiences performance issues multiple times each night. Root-cause analysis identifies sudden CPU-utilization increases lasting 5 minutes on an Amazon EC2 Linux instance. A CloudOps engineer needs to identify the process ID (PID) of the service or process consuming the additional CPU.  
  
What should the CloudOps engineer do to collect process-utilization information with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent procstat plugin to capture CPU process metrics.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to run every minute to capture the PID and send a notification.
Log in to the EC2 instance by using a .pem key each night. Then run the top command.
Use the default Amazon CloudWatch CPU utilization metric to capture the PID in CloudWatch.

questions.explanation:
The Amazon CloudWatch agent `procstat` plugin collects metrics from individual Linux processes, including `cpu_usage` and `pid`. Configuring it provides ongoing per-process utilization data that can identify the CPU-consuming process during recurring spikes, without manual instance access or custom code.

**Learn more:** [Collect process metrics with the procstat plugin - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Agent-procstat-process-metrics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To meet regulatory requirements, a CloudOps engineer must back up an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) to an Amazon S3 bucket. If the CloudOps engineer later restores the AMI from that bucket, it must retain the same AMI image ID as the original AMI.  
  
Which solution satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Create a copy of the AMI. Specify the destination S3 bucket. Set the launch permissions to implicit.
Archive the snapshot that is associated with the AMI. Specify the S3 bucket as the archive destination.
Create a store image task. Specify the image ID and the destination S3 bucket.
Use the AWS CLI copy-image command. Specify the image ID and the destination S3 bucket.

questions.explanation: AWS's store-and-restore-AMI-using-S3 feature lets you create a store image task that archives an AMI as a single object in a specified S3 bucket, and restoring that AMI back in the same Region reassigns it its original AMI ID, which is exactly what's needed to retain the same AMI image ID after backup and restoration.
