A company deploys AWS infrastructure in a VPC with an internet gateway. The VPC contains public and private subnets. An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance is deployed in a private subnet. An AWS Lambda function uses that same private subnet and connects to the DB instance to query data.  
  
A developer updates the Lambda function so it must publish messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. After the update, the Lambda function times out when it attempts to publish messages to the SQS queue.  
  
Which solutions will resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Reconfigure the Lambda function so that the function is not connected to the VPC.
Deploy an RDS proxy. Configure the Lambda function to connect to the DB instance through the proxy.
Deploy a NAT gateway. Update the private subnet's route table to route all traffic to the NAT gateway.
Create an interface endpoint for Amazon SQS in the VPC.
Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS in the VPC.

questions.explanation:
A NAT gateway with a default route from the private subnet provides outbound internet access to the regional Amazon SQS endpoint. An Amazon SQS interface VPC endpoint provides private connectivity to SQS through AWS PrivateLink, without requiring internet or NAT access. Amazon SQS does not support gateway VPC endpoints; those are limited to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.

**Learn more:** [Enable internet access for VPC-connected Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc-internet.html) · [Internetwork traffic privacy in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-internetwork-traffic-privacy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates multiple AWS accounts. A CloudOps engineer uses a sandbox account to create and validate IAM policies that will be used in a production account. The CloudOps engineer deploys policies to the sandbox account for testing by using AWS CloudFormation. After the tests succeed, the CloudOps engineer deploys the policies to production. AWS CloudTrail is configured in both the sandbox and production accounts.  
  
The CloudOps engineer needs to detect any IAM-policy changes after CloudFormation deploys the policies and must receive notifications about every such change.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative effort?

options.text: Configure CloudTrail to send email notifications to the CloudOps engineer when CloudTrail detects changes to the IAM policies.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to check the CloudFormation stack for drift. Configure the function to use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the CloudOps engineer if the function detects any drift.

Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to generate a policy based on CloudTrail activity for the IAM role that is attached to the IAM policies in the production account. Compare the results to the IAM policies that are in the sandbox account. Send a notification to the CloudOps engineer if the policies are different.
Store the IAM policies as a JSON document in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to periodically compare the IAM policies with the JSON document that is stored in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation drift detection identifies resource configuration changes made outside CloudFormation by comparing the actual resource configuration with the configuration expected from the stack template. An Amazon EventBridge rule can invoke a Lambda function to check for stack drift, and the function can publish an Amazon SNS notification when drift is detected. CloudTrail records API activity but does not natively send email notifications, while IAM Access Analyzer does not compare policy versions between accounts.

**Learn more:** [Detect unmanaged configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-stack-drift.html) · [Monitoring CloudFormation and Git sync events with EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/eventbridge-integration.html)

A company’s application is hosted by an internet provider at app.example.com. The company wants to reach the application using www.company.com, which it owns and manages through Amazon Route 53.  
  
Which Route 53 record should be created to accomplish this?

A developer enables versioning on an Amazon S3 bucket. When attempting to perform a write operation on the bucket, the developer receives an HTTP 404 NoSuchKey error.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must resolve this issue.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Disable versioning on the S3 bucket and retry the write operation.
Modify the bucket policy to allow write operations on versioned objects.
Wait at least 15 minutes after enabling versioning, and then perform the write operation.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket.

questions.explanation:
When versioning is enabled on an S3 bucket for the first time, the change can take up to 15 minutes to propagate throughout Amazon S3. During that period, object requests can intermittently return `HTTP 404 NoSuchKey`; AWS recommends waiting 15 minutes before performing write operations such as `PUT` or `DELETE`.

**Learn more:** [Enabling versioning on buckets - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/manage-versioning-examples.html) · [PutBucketVersioning - Amazon S3 API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_PutBucketVersioning.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team needs to match Amazon EventBridge events where an Amazon EC2 instance’s state is not `"terminated"`.  
  
An example event is as follows:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783925910875-zajjrvpf.png)  
  
Which event pattern should the development team use to identify the relevant events?
questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge uses `anything-but` to match every value except the specified one. Nesting `equals-ignore-case` inside `anything-but` excludes `terminated` in any letter casing, while the array containing that comparison object is the required event-pattern structure for the `detail.state` field. [AWS: Comparison operators for EventBridge event patterns](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-pattern-operators.html)

**Learn more:** [Comparison operators for use in event patterns in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-pattern-operators.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer manages a company’s disaster recovery procedures. The company has a source Amazon S3 bucket in a production account and wants to replicate objects from that source to a destination S3 bucket in a nonproduction account. The CloudOps engineer configures S3 cross-Region, cross-account replication to copy the source S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket. When the CloudOps engineer tries to access objects in the destination S3 bucket, they receive an **Access Denied** error.  
  
Which solution will resolve this issue?

options.text: Modify the replication configuration to change object ownership to the destination S3 bucket owner.
Ensure that the replication rule applies to all objects in the source S3 bucket and is not scoped to a single prefix.
Retry the request when the S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) has elapsed.
Verify that the storage class for the replicated objects did not change between the source S3 bucket and the destination S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
For cross-account replication, Amazon S3 retains the source object owner as the replica owner by default. Enabling the replication owner-override setting changes ownership of newly replicated objects to the destination bucket owner, allowing the destination account to control and access those replicas.

**Learn more:** [Changing the replica owner - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-change-owner.html) · [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer monitors and maintains resource availability in an AWS environment. The CloudOps engineer observes that CPU utilization on an Amazon EC2 instance running web server software rises above 80% at different times each day. The CPU spikes align with peak daily traffic. The elevated CPU load has caused customer performance problems.  
  
The CloudOps engineer must resolve the system performance problem without causing any service interruptions.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that invokes an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to vertically scale the EC2 instance when the CPU utilization exceeds 80%.
Configure an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to run a script that automatically restarts the application when CPU utilization exceeds 80%.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Systems Manager Automation document. Configure the document to increase the EC2 instance size when CPU utilization exceeds 80%.
Set up an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that triggers a scaling policy to launch additional EC2 instances when the CPU utilization exceeds 80%.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can use a CloudWatch alarm and scaling policy to add EC2 instances when CPU utilization crosses a threshold. Scaling out adds capacity while the existing instance continues to serve traffic, avoiding the downtime associated with resizing an instance or restarting its application. AWS documents that a breached CloudWatch alarm invokes the associated Auto Scaling policy, which can increase Auto Scaling group capacity.

**Learn more:** [Step and simple scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scaling-simple-step.html) · [Dynamic scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-scale-based-on-demand.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A healthcare company uses Amazon SageMaker in a VPC to develop machine learning (ML) models that use data stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to ensure that SageMaker securely accesses the data without using public IP addresses.  
  
Which solution satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Create Amazon S3 gateway endpoints. Configure SageMaker to access the S3 buckets by using AWS PrivateLink.
Provision a NAT gateway within the same VPC where the company runs SageMaker. Configure SageMaker to access the S3 buckets by using the NAT gateway.
Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to connect SageMaker to the S3 buckets.
Configure AWS Transit Gateway to route traffic from SageMaker to the S3 buckets.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoints provide private connectivity from a VPC to S3 without an internet gateway or NAT device. For SageMaker training jobs that need to reach S3 buckets from a VPC without internet access, AWS directs users to create an S3 VPC endpoint and select the Gateway type; the endpoint adds the S3 route to the selected route tables. Gateway endpoints are distinct from AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints, but the S3 gateway endpoint named in the selected choice is the applicable mechanism.

**Learn more:** [Give SageMaker AI Training Jobs Access to Resources in Your Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-vpc.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has millions of subscribers. Its marketing department wants to automate a process that sends notifications to subscribers every Saturday. The company already has a mechanism that uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send notifications to subscribers. However, the company has historically sent notifications to subscribers manually.  
  
A CloudOps engineer needs a solution to send notifications automatically on a schedule.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient way?

options.text: Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a cron job to use the AWS SDK to send an SNS notification to subscribers every Saturday.
Create a rule in Amazon EventBridge that triggers every Saturday. Configure the rule to publish a notification to an SNS topic.
Create an SNS subscription to a message fanout that sends notifications to subscribers every Saturday.
Use the AWS Step Functions scheduling feature to run a Step Functions step every Saturday. Configure the step to publish a message to an SNS topic.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule can use a cron expression to run every Saturday and invoke an Amazon SNS topic as its target. This provides fully managed, schedule-based publishing without operating an instance or building an unnecessary workflow. [Creating a scheduled rule in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-schedule.html)

**Learn more:** [Creating a scheduled rule in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-schedule.html) · [Setting a schedule pattern for scheduled rules in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-scheduled-rule-pattern.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer must ensure that AWS resources in multiple AWS accounts receive consistent tags. The company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage the accounts centrally. The company needs to implement cost allocation tags to accurately track costs allocated to each business unit.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use Organizations tag policies to enforce mandatory tagging on all resources. Enable cost allocation tags in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console.
Configure AWS CloudTrail events to invoke an AWS Lambda function to detect untagged resources and to automatically assign tags based on predefined rules.
Use AWS Config to evaluate tagging compliance. Use AWS Budgets to apply tags for cost allocation.
Use AWS Service Catalog to provision only pre-tagged resources. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to enforce tagging across the organization.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations tag policies centrally standardize tag keys and values across organizational accounts and can prevent noncompliant tagging operations for supported resource types. Activating the applicable user-defined tag keys in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console makes them available for cost allocation, so costs can be tracked by business-unit tag. This avoids maintaining custom event-driven remediation or separate compliance tooling.

**Learn more:** [AWS Organizations Tag Policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies.html) · [Activating User-Defined Cost Allocation Tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/activating-tags.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a stateless application consisting of a web server and a PostgreSQL database on one Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance becomes overloaded during periods of high application traffic, resulting in slow response times.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must implement a solution to address the application's performance issues. The solution must support increased application traffic as the user count continues to grow. It must also make the application highly available.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Specify the EC2 instance as the origin.
Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling group of web servers behind an Application Load Balancer.
Upgrade the existing EC2 instance to a larger instance type with more CPU and memory resources.
Use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ deployment for the database. Point the application to the new endpoint.
Upgrade the PostgreSQL database on the EC2 instance to a newer version.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer distributing requests to web servers in an EC2 Auto Scaling group provides horizontal scaling for the stateless web tier and redundant capacity. Moving PostgreSQL to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ deployment separates database processing from the web-server instance and provides high availability through a standby database and failover endpoint.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/what-is-amazon-ec2-auto-scaling.html) · [Multi-AZ deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.html)

options.text: Edit the private subnet to change the CIDR block to /27.
Edit the private subnet to extend across a second Availability Zone.
Assign additional Elastic IP addresses to the private subnet.
Create a new private subnet to hold the required EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS reserves five IPv4 addresses in every subnet. A /28 subnet therefore provides 11 usable addresses, so 11 EC2 instances exhaust its private IP capacity. An existing subnet’s CIDR block cannot be changed, and every subnet is limited to one Availability Zone. Creating another private subnet with an available, non-overlapping CIDR block provides addresses for the additional instances.

**Learn more:** [Subnet CIDR blocks - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/subnet-sizing.html) · [CreateSubnet - Amazon EC2 API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateSubnet.html)

A CloudOps engineer maintains a web application that uses an Amazon CloudFront web distribution, an Application Load Balancer (ALB), Amazon RDS, and Amazon EC2 in a VPC. Logging is enabled for all services. The CloudOps engineer must investigate HTTP Layer 7 status codes from the web application.  
  
Which log sources contain the status codes? (Choose two.)

options.text: VPC Flow Logs
AWS CloudTrail logs
ALB access logs
CloudFront access logs
RDS logs

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer access logs include `elb_status_code` for the response generated by the load balancer and `target_status_code` for the response from the target. CloudFront access logs include the viewer-facing HTTP status code in the `sc-status` field.

**Learn more:** [Access logs for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html) · [Standard logging reference - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/standard-logs-reference.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer creates a new VPC containing a private subnet, a security group that permits all outbound traffic, and an Amazon EC2 Instance Connect endpoint in a private subnet. The CloudOps engineer associates the security group with EC2 Instance Connect.  
  
The CloudOps engineer launches an EC2 instance from an Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI) in the private subnet. The CloudOps engineer associates the instance with the same subnet that the security group uses. The CloudOps engineer launches the EC2 instance without an SSH key pair.  
  
The CloudOps engineer attempts to connect to the instance by using the EC2 Instance Connect endpoint. However, the connection fails.  
  
How can the CloudOps engineer connect to the instance?

options.text: Create an inbound rule in the security group to allow HTTPS traffic on port 443 from the private subnet.
Create an inbound rule in the security group to allow SSH traffic on port 22 from the private subnet.
Create an IAM instance profile that allows AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to access the EC2 instance. Associate the instance profile with the instance.
Recreate the EC2 instance. Associate an SSH key pair with the instance.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint requires the target instance’s security group to allow inbound SSH traffic on TCP port 22 from the endpoint. When client IP preservation is off, the traffic source is the endpoint network interface address, which is allocated from its subnet; allowing SSH from the private subnet therefore permits the connection. EC2 Instance Connect supplies an ephemeral SSH key, so an EC2 launch key pair is unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Security groups for EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/eice-security-groups.html) · [Connect to an Amazon EC2 instance using EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/connect-using-eice.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to use AWS Systems Manager to manage a large fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The company hosts the instances in private subnets and follows the principle of least privilege when assigning access permissions. All private subnets have internet connectivity through a NAT gateway.  
  
A CloudOps engineer installs the latest version of the Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent). However, the EC2 instances do not show up in Systems Manager Fleet Manager. The CloudOps engineer must fix this issue.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance that is deployed in the public subnet. Update the private subnet's route table to use the NAT instance.
Create a VPC endpoint for Systems Manager. Remove routes to the internet through the NAT gateway from the private subnet's route table.
Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore AWS managed policy to the EC2 instance profile that is associated with the instances.
Attach a custom policy that allows all actions to ssm* to the EC2 instance profile that is associated with the instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 instances must have an IAM instance profile that allows SSM Agent to communicate with AWS Systems Manager. `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore` supplies the required managed-node permissions while adhering to least privilege. The existing NAT gateway already provides the outbound connectivity needed to reach Systems Manager service endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting managed node availability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/fleet-manager-troubleshooting-managed-nodes.html) · [Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/setup-instance-permissions.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company intends to migrate several high-performance computing (HPC) virtual machines (VMs) to Amazon EC2 instances on AWS. A CloudOps engineer must select a placement group for this deployment. The strategy must minimize network latency and maximize network throughput between the HPC VMs.  
  
Which strategy should the CloudOps engineer select to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the instances in a cluster placement group in one Availability Zone.
Deploy the instances in a partition placement group in two Availability Zones.
Deploy the instances in a partition placement group in one Availability Zone.
Deploy the instances in a spread placement group in two Availability Zones.

questions.explanation:
A cluster placement group packs EC2 instances close together in a single Availability Zone, providing the low-latency, high-throughput networking needed for tightly coupled HPC communication.

**Learn more:** [Placement strategies for your placement groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)

A company uses AWS Lambda to process files that users upload to an Amazon S3 bucket. When a user uploads a file to the S3 bucket, S3 Event Notifications invokes a Lambda function to process that file.  
  
The company wants to automatically invoke the Lambda function only for files with a `.txt` extension that users upload to the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure a Lambda function that is invoked by S3 PUT requests for .txt files in the S3 bucket.
Configure a Lambda function that is invoked by S3 GET requests for .txt files in the S3 bucket.

Configure an S3 bucket notification to send all object creation events to an Amazon SNS topic. Subscribe the Lambda function to the SNS topic. Apply a filter policy on the SNS topic for .txt file extensions.
Modify the existing S3 Event Notifications configuration to send events for .txt file uploads to Amazon CloudWatch Logs to invoke the existing Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 event notifications can invoke a Lambda function for `s3:ObjectCreated:Put` events and can filter by an object key’s suffix. Configuring a `.txt` suffix filter on the S3 PUT event ensures that only uploaded `.txt` objects invoke the function.

**Learn more:** [Configuring event notifications using object key name filtering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-filtering.html) · [Event notification types and destinations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html)

A finance company keeps confidential data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses Amazon QuickSight to analyze that data and create dashboard reports. The company requires that all data access and connections to QuickSight stay within the company's VPC network boundary.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for QuickSight. Configure the endpoint to connect to QuickSight within the VPC by using AWS PrivateLink. Create a manifest file that points to the S3 data. Grant QuickSight permission to access the S3 bucket.

Set up a VPC endpoint for QuickSight. Use an Amazon EC2 instance as a proxy to establish a direct connection between the VPC and QuickSight. Create a manifest file that points to the S3 data. Store the manifest on the EC2 instance. Grant QuickSight permission to access the EC2 instance.
Configure an Amazon S3 VPC gateway endpoint. Route all data from QuickSight through the endpoint to transfer data. Grant QuickSight permission to access the S3 bucket.
Configure a NAT gateway in the company’s VPC. Route all data from QuickSight through the NAT gateway to transfer data. Grant QuickSight permission to access the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon QuickSight interface VPC endpoint, powered by AWS PrivateLink, provides private connectivity between the VPC and QuickSight without requiring public internet access. An S3 manifest file identifies the S3 data for the QuickSight data source, and QuickSight must be granted permission to read the bucket and referenced objects. [Quick interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/developerguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html) [Run queries with Amazon S3 data sources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksuite/latest/userguide/datasource-run-as-role.html)

**Learn more:** [Quick interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/developerguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html) · [Run queries with Amazon S3 data sources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksuite/latest/userguide/datasource-run-as-role.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company creates an AWS Lambda function using the default settings. The function must access an Amazon RDS database located in a private subnet of a VPC. The function has the required IAM permissions to access the database. The private subnet has suitable routing configured and can be reached from within the VPC. However, the Lambda function cannot connect to the RDS instance.  
  
What is the most likely reason that the Lambda function cannot connect to the RDS instance?

options.text: The company did not set the RDS instance as the destination for the Lambda function in the function configuration.
The Lambda function configuration did not deploy the function in the same VPC that contains the RDS instance.
The VPC where the Lambda function is deployed is not peered with the VPC where the RDS instance is deployed.
The security group for the Lambda function does not allow outbound access to the RDS instance.

questions.explanation:
A Lambda function created with default settings is not attached to a customer VPC. To connect to an Amazon RDS instance in a private subnet, the function must be configured with VPC subnets and security groups that provide network reachability to that database.

**Learn more:** [AWS Lambda Developer Guide: Connecting a function to a VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company keeps critical data in Amazon S3 buckets. A CloudOps engineer needs to create a solution that records all S3 API activity.  
  
Which action fulfills this requirement?

options.text: Configure S3 bucket metrics to record object access logs.
Create an AWS CloudTrail trail to log data events for all S3 objects.
Enable S3 server access logging for each S3 bucket.
Use AWS IAM Access Analyzer for Amazon S3 to store object access logs.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail data events record Amazon S3 object-level API operations, including read and write activity. Configuring a CloudTrail trail to log data events for all S3 objects provides an auditable record of that activity. CloudTrail trails do not log data events by default, so data-event logging must be explicitly enabled.

**Learn more:** [Logging data events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/logging-data-events-with-cloudtrail.html) · [Enabling CloudTrail event logging for S3 buckets and objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/enable-cloudtrail-logging-for-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer has an AWS CloudFormation template for the company’s existing infrastructure in `us-west-2`. The engineer tries to use the template to create a new stack in `eu-west-1`, but the stack deploys only partially, returns an error message, and then rolls back.  
  
Why might this template fail to deploy? (Choose two.)

options.text: The template referenced an IAM user that is not available in eu-west-1.
The template referenced an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that is not available in eu-west-1.
The template did not have the proper level of permissions to deploy the resources.
The template requested services that do not exist in eu-west-1.
CloudFormation templates can be used only to update existing services

questions.explanation:
Amazon Machine Image IDs are regional; an AMI referenced from `us-west-2` may not be available in `eu-west-1`. CloudFormation resource availability can also differ by AWS Region, so a template can fail when it requests services or resource types unavailable in the target Region.

**Learn more:** [CloudFormation template Mappings syntax](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/mappings-section-structure.html) · [CloudFormation resource specification](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/cfn-resource-specification.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer must turn off automatic backups for an Amazon RDS instance to reduce costs. When attempting to disable backups, the engineer receives an error stating that the retention period must be from 1 to 35.  
  
What is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The RDS instance has insufficient permissions to change the backup retention period.
Read replicas are configured for the RDS instance.
The RDS instance is using the default backup window.
The RDS instance is part of a Multi-AZ deployment.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon RDS DB instance that serves as the source of read replicas must have automated backups enabled. Its backup retention period therefore cannot be set to 0, which disables automated backups; it must remain between 1 and 35 days.

**Learn more:** [Backup retention period - Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_WorkingWithAutomatedBackups.BackupRetention.html) · [promote-read-replica - AWS CLI Command Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/rds/promote-read-replica.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has users who deploy Amazon EC2 instances with more volume performance capacity than they need. A CloudOps engineer must review all Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes associated with those instances and create cost-optimization recommendations based on IOPS and throughput.  
  
What should the CloudOps engineer do to meet these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient way?

options.text: Use the monitoring graphs in the EC2 console to view metrics for EBS volumes. Review the consumed space against the provisioned space on each volume. Identify any volumes that have low utilization.
Stop the EC2 instances from the EC2 console. Change the EC2 instance type to Amazon EBS-optimized. Start the EC2 instances.
Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer. Allow sufficient time for metrics to be gathered. Review the Compute Optimizer findings for EBS volumes.

Install the fio tool onto the EC2 instances and create a .cfg file to approximate the required workloads. Use the benchmark results to gauge whether the provisioned EBS volumes are of the most appropriate type.

questions.explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer generates Amazon EBS volume recommendations by analyzing utilization metrics. Its recommendations include appropriate volume type, size, IOPS, throughput, pricing, and savings information, allowing EBS volumes to be assessed at scale for performance right-sizing and cost optimization.

**Learn more:** [Viewing Amazon EBS volume recommendations - AWS Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/view-ebs-recommendations.html) · [EBS volume metrics - AWS Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/ebs-metrics-analyzed.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has introduced a security policy requiring every Amazon EBS volume to be encrypted at rest. The company must use a custom key policy to control access to the encryption keys, and it must rotate the keys annually.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create AWS KMS symmetric customer managed keys. Enable automatic key rotation.
Use AWS owned AWS KMS keys across the company's AWS environment.
Create AWS KMS asymmetric customer managed keys. Enable automatic key rotation.
Create AWS KMS symmetric customer managed keys by using imported key material. Rotate the keys on a yearly basis.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS supports only symmetric KMS keys. A symmetric customer managed KMS key supports a custom key policy and AWS KMS automatic key rotation; the default automatic rotation period is 365 days. This provides the required annual rotation without manual key-material management. Asymmetric KMS keys are not supported for EBS encryption, and keys with imported material cannot use automatic rotation.

**Learn more:** [Data protection in Amazon EBS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/data-protection.html) · [Enable automatic key rotation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotating-keys-enable.html)

A CloudOps engineer must implement a monitoring system that collects instance metrics every minute for an application. The application runs on a highly available pair of Amazon EC2 instances. The monitoring system must send an email alert when the metrics exceed a predefined threshold.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use the AWS Health Dashboard to extract the instance metrics. Configure Amazon EventBridge to detect and react to changes in the metrics and to send email alerts.
Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the instances. Copy the logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an AWS Lambda function to send email alerts based on the logs from the S3 bucket.
Use basic monitoring in Amazon CloudWatch for the instance metrics. Configure CloudWatch alarms that use Amazon SNS to send email alerts.
Use detailed monitoring in Amazon CloudWatch for the instance metrics. Configure CloudWatch alarms that use Amazon SNS to send email alerts.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 detailed monitoring publishes CloudWatch metrics at one-minute intervals. A CloudWatch alarm can evaluate a metric against a defined threshold and notify an Amazon SNS topic, which can send an email notification.

**Learn more:** [Manage detailed monitoring for your EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/manage-detailed-monitoring.html) · [Using Amazon CloudWatch alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/AlarmThatSendsEmail.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A school uses a web application to record student attendance. The application uses an Amazon API Gateway REST API and backend AWS Lambda functions. It stores data in an Amazon DynamoDB table configured for on-demand capacity mode.  
  
Teachers report slow application performance at the same time each weekday. A CloudOps engineer observes that the performance issue occurs only when application demand rises suddenly. The application can support the peak load when demand increases gradually. The CloudOps engineer must modify the application to fix the performance issue.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency with scheduled auto scaling for the Lambda functions.
Configure reserved concurrency with scheduled auto scaling for the Lambda functions.
Change the DynamoDB table from on-demand capacity mode to provisioned capacity mode with auto scaling.
Change the DynamoDB table from on-demand capacity mode to provisioned capacity mode. Set the provisioned capacity to match peak usage.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB on-demand capacity instantly supports up to twice a table’s previous traffic peak, but a sudden increase beyond that level can be throttled while additional capacity is allocated. Provisioning capacity to match the known peak makes the required read and write throughput available before the predictable weekday surge begins. DynamoDB auto scaling responds after demand changes and can throttle requests during its adjustment period.

**Learn more:** [DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/on-demand-capacity-mode.html) · [Managing throughput capacity automatically with DynamoDB auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/AutoScaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deploys an application hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. For security, the instances reside in a private subnet.  
  
An application team requires SSH access to the instances from corporate desktops in an office. The desktops have internet connectivity.  
  
Which solution provides this access?

options.text: Configure a NAT gateway in the public subnet.
Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises network and the VPC.
Configure an internet gateway. Attach the internet gateway to the VPC.
Create security groups that allow inbound traffic from the on-premises network to resources in the public subnets.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates private network connectivity between the on-premises corporate network and the VPC, enabling corporate desktops to reach the EC2 instances’ private IP addresses for SSH. The VPC route tables and instance security group must permit the VPN-routed traffic. A NAT gateway supports outbound access from private subnets and does not enable inbound SSH access.

**Learn more:** [Get started with AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/SetUpVPNConnections.html) · [Prerequisites for EC2 Instance Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-connect-prerequisites.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer has blocked public access for all company Amazon S3 buckets. The engineer wants to receive a notification if an S3 bucket becomes publicly readable in the future.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient way to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically checks the public access settings for each S3 bucket. Set up Amazon SNS to send notifications.
Create a cron script that uses the S3 API to check the public access settings for each S3 bucket. Set up Amazon SNS to send notifications.
Enable S3 Event Notifications for each S3 bucket. Subscribe S3 Event Notifications to an Amazon SNS topic.
Enable the s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited managed rule in AWS Config. Subscribe the AWS Config rule to an Amazon SNS topic.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Config managed rule `s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited` detects whether an S3 bucket permits public read access by evaluating Block Public Access settings, bucket policies, and bucket ACLs. It is triggered by configuration changes, and AWS Config can send compliance-state notifications to an Amazon SNS topic, providing managed detection and alerting without custom polling code.

**Learn more:** [s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited - AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited.html) · [Notifications that AWS Config Sends to an Amazon SNS topic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/notifications-for-AWS-Config.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer has an Amazon S3 bucket and a new AWS Lambda function. The engineer attempts to configure a new event notification from the S3 bucket to the Lambda function by using the Lambda console. The configuration fails and returns this error: "Unable to validate the following destination configurations."  
  
The engineer confirms that the new Lambda function and the function's IAM role are correctly configured.  
  
What causes this error?

options.text: The maximum number of S3 event notification destinations has been exceeded for the S3 bucket.
The S3 bucket owner needs to grant the Lambda function explicit cross-account permissions by using a resource policy.
The new Lambda function's resource-based policy is missing the lambda:InvokeFunction permission for Amazon S3.
The S3 bucket has an existing stale event notification that points to a deleted or permission-deficient resource.

questions.explanation:
When an Amazon S3 event-notification configuration is added or updated, S3 validates both the new destination and existing destinations that remain configured. A stale notification targeting a deleted resource, or a resource whose resource-based policy no longer allows S3 to deliver events, causes destination validation to fail.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot errors when you create Amazon S3 Event Notifications](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/lambda-invoke-error-s3-bucket-permission) · [Using Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, and Lambda for S3 event notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/how-to-enable-disable-notification-intro.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a large number of Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances for business functions such as ordering, fulfillment, and billing. The company uses AWS Systems Manager to administer the EC2 instances. The company needs to ensure that the Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) always remains updated to the latest version.  
  
Which solution will satisfy this requirement in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Enable the Auto update SSM Agent setting in Systems Manager Fleet Manager.

Subscribe to SSM Agent notifications on Github. Configure the subscription events to invoke an Amazon SNS topic. Configure the SNS topic to run a custom AWS Lambda function to update the SSM Agent by using the Systems Manager Run Command API.
Enable the Auto update SSM Agent setting in Systems Manager Patch Manager.

Subscribe to SSM Agent notifications on Github. Configure the subscription events to invoke an Amazon SNS topic. Configure the topic to run a custom AWS Lambda function to update the SSM Agent by using a Systems Manager Automation document.

questions.explanation:
Fleet Manager’s **Auto update SSM Agent** setting is the AWS-recommended one-click mechanism for all managed nodes in an account. Systems Manager checks for new SSM Agent versions and automatically installs the latest released version, avoiding custom notification, Lambda, and update orchestration components.

**Learn more:** [Automating updates to SSM Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/ssm-agent-automatic-updates.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is experiencing an increase in production incidents. A CloudOps engineer must give developers secure access to Amazon EC2 instances from the AWS Management Console. The developers must be able to connect successfully by using EC2 Instance Connect for real-time troubleshooting.  
  
The EC2 instances use the latest Amazon Linux 2023 AMIs. The EC2 instances are publicly accessible. The EC2 instances have correctly configured security groups that permit inbound SSH traffic. The developers will use the default `ec2-user` account to access the instances from the console.  
  
Which step should the CloudOps engineer perform **NEXT** to ensure that the developers can successfully connect by using EC2 Instance Connect?

options.text: Create an IAM role with EC2 access. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
Download and install the EC2 Instance Connect agent on the production instances.
Grant IAM permissions to the developers to use EC2 Instance Connect and describe the EC2 instances.
Enable AWS CloudTrail logging. Create a VPC endpoint for EC2 Instance Connect.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Linux 2023 AMIs include EC2 Instance Connect, and the network prerequisites for direct SSH access are already satisfied. Each developer’s IAM identity must be allowed to call `ec2-instance-connect:SendSSHPublicKey` so EC2 Instance Connect can publish its temporary SSH key, and it must have `ec2:DescribeInstances` to view and select the instance in the EC2 console.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Complete the configuration required to connect to your instance using EC2 Instance Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-connect-tutorial.html) · [EC2InstanceConnect AWS managed policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/EC2InstanceConnect.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A multinational company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage more than 200 member accounts across multiple AWS Regions. The company must make sure that every AWS resource complies with specific security requirements.  
  
The company must not deploy any EC2 instances in the `ap-southeast-2` Region. The company must fully block root user actions in every member account. The company must stop any user, including administrators, from deleting AWS CloudTrail logs.  
  
The company needs a centrally managed solution that it can automatically apply to all current and future accounts.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create AWS Config rules with remediation actions in each account to detect policy violations. Implement IAM permissions boundaries for the account root users.

Enable AWS Security Hub across the organization. Create custom security standards to enforce the security requirements. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the standards to all the accounts in the organization. Set up Security Hub automated remediation actions.
Use AWS Control Tower for account governance. Configure Region deny controls. Use service control policies (SCPs) to restrict root user access.
Configure AWS Firewall Manager with security policies to meet the security requirements. Use an AWS Config aggregator with organization-wide conformance packs to detect security policy violations.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower supplies centrally managed preventive controls for AWS Organizations. Its Region deny control blocks operations outside selected governed Regions; its root-user control uses an SCP to deny all actions by member-account root principals; and its mandatory CloudTrail protection denies `cloudtrail:DeleteTrail` and other trail configuration changes. Applied through the organization’s OU structure, these controls govern existing member accounts and accounts added in the future.

**Learn more:** [Configure the Region deny control - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/region-deny.html) · [Strongly recommended controls with preventive behavior - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/strongly-recommended-preventive-controls.html)

A company uses AWS CloudFormation to manage a stack of Amazon EC2 instances in AWS. A CloudOps engineer must preserve the instances and all their data, even if somebody deletes the stack.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set the DeletionPolicy attribute to Snapshot for the EC2 instance resource in the CloudFormation template.
Automate backups by using Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM).
Create a backup plan in AWS Backup.
Set the DeletionPolicy attribute to Retain for the EC2 instance resource in the CloudFormation template.

questions.explanation:
The `Retain` `DeletionPolicy` causes AWS CloudFormation to keep an EC2 instance and its contents when the stack is deleted. `Snapshot` is intended for snapshot-capable resources such as `AWS::EC2::Volume`, rather than an EC2 instance resource.

**Learn more:** [DeletionPolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage multiple AWS accounts. The company must send particular events from every account in the organization to a new receiver account, where an AWS Lambda function will process the events.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must configure Amazon EventBridge to route the events to a target event bus in the `us-west-2` Region of the new receiver account. The CloudOps engineer creates rules in the sender accounts and in the receiver account that match the specified events. The rules do not include an account parameter in the event pattern. The CloudOps engineer creates IAM roles in the sender accounts that allow `PutEvents` actions on the target event bus.  
  
The first test events, which originate in the `us-east-1` Region, are not processed by the Lambda function in the receiving account.  
  
What is the most likely reason that the events are not processed?

options.text: Interface VPC endpoints for EventBridge are required in the sender accounts and receiver accounts.
The target Lambda function is in a different AWS Region, which is not supported by EventBridge.
The resource-based policy on the target event bus must be modified to allow PutEvents API calls from the sender accounts.
The rule in the receiving account must specify {

questions.explanation:
A receiving EventBridge event bus must have a resource-based policy that authorizes `events:PutEvents` from the sender accounts or from the AWS Organization. An IAM role in each sender account grants the sender-side permission but does not itself permit the target event bus to accept cross-account events.

**Learn more:** [Sending and receiving events between AWS accounts in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-cross-account.html) · [Permissions for event buses in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-event-bus-perms.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage multiple AWS accounts. To meet regulatory requirements, the company deploys workload environments in five AWS Regions. The company uses a separate AWS account for each Region.  
  
The company must connect every environment’s VPC to a central shared VPC that provides directory services and to a shared monitoring VPC. Each shared account is in a separate AWS account.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a transit gateway in the central shared AWS account. Share the transit gateway with the company's AWS accounts. Connect all VPCs to the central transit gateway.

Create a separate transit gateway in every Region where the company has deployed resources. Share the transit gateways with company's AWS accounts. Connect the VPC in each Region to the transit gateway that is in the same Region. Peer the transit gateways. Create appropriate routes in all route tables.

Create a virtual private gateway for the shared VPCs. Create a customer gateway for the workload VPCs. Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the directory VPC, the monitoring VPC, and every workload VPC.
Create VPC peering connections between the central shared VPC, the shared monitoring VPC, and every workload VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is a Regional virtual router, so VPCs attach to a transit gateway in the same Region. A transit gateway in every deployed Region, shared with the relevant AWS accounts, provides local VPC connectivity. Transit gateway peering supports routing between gateways in different Regions, and the required static routes in transit gateway and VPC route tables enable connectivity among all regional workload VPCs and the shared VPCs.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html) · [Transit gateway peering attachments in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-peering.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s website is hosted on an Amazon EC2 Linux instance. The website must serve PDF files from an Amazon S3 bucket. Public access to the S3 bucket is blocked at the account level. The company must enable website users to download the PDF files.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative effort?

options.text: Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows s3:list* and s3:get* permissions. Assign the role to the EC2 instance. Assign a company employee to download requested PDF file to the EC2 instance and to deliver the files to website users. Create an AWS Lambda function to periodically delete local files.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses an origin access control (OAC) that points to the S3 bucket. Apply a bucket policy to the bucket to allow connections from the CloudFront distribution. Assign a company employee to provide a download URL that contains the distribution URL and the object path to users when users request PDF files.
Change the S3 bucket permissions to allow public access on the source S3 bucket. Assign a company employee to provide a PDF file URL to users when users request the PDF files.
Deploy an EC2 instance that has an 1AM instance profile to a public subnet. Use a signed URL from the EC2 instance to provide temporary access to the S3 bucket for website users.

questions.explanation:
A CloudFront distribution using an S3 origin protected by origin access control (OAC) allows CloudFront to retrieve objects from a private bucket when the bucket policy authorizes that specific distribution. Users can download the objects through CloudFront URLs without enabling public S3 access or managing files on EC2. AWS recommends OAC for restricting an S3 origin to CloudFront distributions.

**Learn more:** [Restrict access to an Amazon S3 origin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html) · [Restrict access to files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-overview.html)

options.text: Change the launch configuration to use a larger instance size.
Increase the minimum number of instances in the Auto Scaling group.
Add a predictive scaling policy to the Auto Scaling group.
Add a warm pool to the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling warm pool keeps pre-initialized instances alongside the Auto Scaling group. During scale-out, the group can draw from that pool so the instances avoid a full cold-start initialization, reducing latency caused by long-running boot scripts. Warm pools are specifically intended to reduce long boot-time latency without overprovisioning the Auto Scaling group.

**Learn more:** [Decrease latency for applications with long boot times using warm pools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html)

A CloudOps engineer is troubleshooting an Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics implementation. CloudWatch Synthetics results must be delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
The CloudOps engineer copied the configuration from an existing canary that runs in a VPC with an attached internet gateway. However, the engineer cannot successfully start the canary in a private VPC with no internet access.  
  
What should the CloudOps engineer do to run the canary successfully in the private VPC?

options.text: Ensure that the DNS resolution option and the DNS hostnames option are turned on in the VPC. Add the synthetics:GetCanaryRuns permission to the VPC. On the S3 bucket, add the IgnorePublicAcls permission to the CloudWatch Synthetics role.

Ensure that the DNS resolution option and the DNS hostnames option are turned off in the VPC. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Add the permissions to allow CloudWatch Synthetics to use the S3 endpoint.

Ensure that the DNS resolution option and the DNS hostnames option are turned off in the VPAdd a security group to the canary to allow outbound traffic on the DNS port. Add the permissions to allow CloudWatch Synthetics to write to the S3 bucket.

Ensure that the DNS resolution option and the DNS hostnames option are turned on in the VPC. Create an interface VPC endpoint for CloudWatch. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Add the permissions to allow CloudWatch Synthetics to use both endpoints.

questions.explanation:
A CloudWatch Synthetics canary in a VPC without internet access needs private access to CloudWatch for metrics and to Amazon S3 for artifacts. AWS requires both DNS resolution and DNS hostnames to be enabled in the VPC. An interface VPC endpoint for CloudWatch and a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 provide that private connectivity, and their policies must permit the canary’s required access.

**Learn more:** [Running a canary on a VPC - Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch_Synthetics_Canaries_VPC.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3 - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s VPC is connected to an on-premises data center by using an AWS Site-to-Site VPN. The company requires Amazon EC2 instances in the VPC to send DNS queries for `example.com` to the DNS servers in the data center.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. Create a conditional forwarding rule on the on-premises DNS servers to forward DNS requests for example.com to the inbound endpoints.
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. Create a forwarding rule on the resolver that sends all queries for example.com to the on-premises DNS servers. Associate this rule with the VPC.
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Create a conditional forwarding rule on the on-premises DNS servers to forward DNS requests for example.com to the outbound endpoints.
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Create a forwarding rule on the resolver that sends all queries for example.com to the on-premises DNS servers. Associate this rule with the VPC.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint forwards DNS queries that originate in a VPC to DNS resolvers on a connected on-premises network. A forwarding rule for `example.com`, associated with the VPC and configured with the on-premises DNS servers as targets, directs those matching EC2-originated queries through that outbound endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Forwarding outbound DNS queries to your network - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-outbound-queries.html) · [Resolving DNS queries between VPCs and your network - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-overview-DSN-queries-to-vpc.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A CloudOps engineer is pursuing cost savings for a company. The engineer identifies several unused Elastic IP addresses. The addresses are distributed across different accounts and AWS Regions within an organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
The CloudOps engineer must manage and track the addresses according to security domains. The engineer must also be able to view the history of assigned addresses.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable AWS Config with an IP address tracking rule.
Use Amazon CloudWatch with custom IP metrics to view addresses by account and Region.
Enable Amazon VPC IP Address Manager for Organizations integrations.
In AWS Systems Manager Inventory, enable a resource data sync to Amazon S3 for IP tracking.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM), when integrated with AWS Organizations, provides centralized IP address management across member accounts and AWS Regions. IPAM scopes can separate address management by security domain, and IPAM retains searchable address-history records for Elastic IP addresses for up to three years.

**Learn more:** [Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) and AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-ipam.html) · [View IP address history](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/ipam/view-history-cidr-ipam.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs production and non-production workloads on hundreds of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances. AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed and configured on the EC2 instances.  
  
During a recent instance patching operation, some instances were not patched because they were either busy or down. The company needs to produce a report listing the current patch version for every instance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Use Systems Manager Inventory to collect patch versions. Generate a report of all instances.
Use Systems Manager Run Command to remotely collect patch version information. Generate a report of all instances.
Use AWS Config to track EC2 instance configuration changes by using output from the SSM Agents. Create a custom rule to check for patch versions. Generate a report of all unpatched instances.

Use AWS Config to monitor the patch status of the EC2 instances by using output from the SSM Agents. Create a configuration compliance rule to check whether patches are installed. Generate a report of all instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Inventory centrally collects metadata from managed nodes and supports querying and reporting across the fleet. Its periodic inventory collection avoids requiring every instance to be reachable for a new Run Command invocation, making it the efficient mechanism for reporting installed patch/version information after some instances missed a patch operation. AWS Config is primarily for configuration history and compliance evaluation, not the direct fleet inventory-reporting mechanism required here.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Inventory](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-inventory.html) · [Generating CSV patch compliance reports](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-store-compliance-results-in-s3.html)

A company operates a web-based application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the us-east-1 Region. Users worldwide access the application. Users outside North America experience high latency and inconsistent application performance. The company must enhance latency and application performance for all global users.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use AWS Global Accelerator in front of the ALB.
Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the ALB.
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB).
Configure Amazon Route 53 health checks to failover between AWS Regions based on latency thresholds.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator directs users to static anycast IP addresses at the nearest edge location and carries traffic over the AWS global network to the Application Load Balancer. This reduces internet-path latency and improves the consistency of application performance for globally distributed users.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html)

A CloudOps engineer is designing a solution for an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The database credentials must be stored and rotated every month. Applications connecting to the DB instance generate write-intensive traffic with variable client connections that can sometimes rise substantially in a short time.  
  
Which solution should the CloudOps engineer select to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to automatically rotate the keys for the DB instance. Use RDS Proxy to handle the increases in database connections.
Configure AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to automatically rotate the keys for the DB instance. Use RDS read replicas to handle the increases in database connections.
Configure AWS Secrets Manager to automatically rotate the credentials for the DB instance. Use RDS Proxy to handle the increases in database connections.
Configure AWS Secrets Manager to automatically rotate the credentials for the DB instance. Use RDS read replicas to handle the increases in database connections.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager securely stores database credentials and supports automated credential rotation on a schedule. Amazon RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, helping applications scale through unpredictable connection surges. RDS read replicas are intended to offload read traffic and do not scale write-intensive workloads on the primary instance.

**Learn more:** [Password management with Amazon RDS and AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-secrets-manager.html) · [Amazon RDS Proxy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a software-as-a-service (SaaS) application. It has integrated the application with AWS services by using the AWS SDK and an IAM user’s access key ID and secret access key.  
  
The company needs to apply the principle of least privilege to the IAM user and must avoid using permanent credentials.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the application to use the AWS STS AssumeRoleWithSAML API operation.
Migrate the application to use the AWS STS AssumeRole API operation. Allow the IAM user to call only AWS STS.
Add a policy to the existing IAM user to scope the permissions to only the permissions that the user needs for the application.
Add an IAM group to scope the permissions to only the permissions that the user needs for the application. Add the IAM user to the IAM group.

questions.explanation:
AWS STS `AssumeRole` returns temporary security credentials. The IAM user can be limited to calling only `sts:AssumeRole`, and the assumed role can contain only the permissions the application requires. This limits direct IAM-user permissions while using short-lived role credentials for AWS service access.

**Learn more:** [AssumeRole — AWS Security Token Service API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html) · [Create a role to give permissions to an IAM user](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an Amazon S3 bucket with server-side encryption using AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) enabled. Several applications read from the S3 bucket for daily reporting. The company clears the data in the S3 bucket each week when it moves the data into a data warehouse.  
  
As additional applications read from the S3 bucket, the cost of KMS-related transactions is increasing. A CloudOps engineer must reduce KMS costs without removing S3 encryption or losing access to existing objects.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Enable S3 Bucket Keys on the S3 bucket. Specify the existing KMS key.
Change the encryption type on the S3 bucket to server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
Use Amazon CloudFront to cache the objects in the S3 bucket and to serve the objects to the applications.
Configure the applications to connect to the S3 bucket through an S3 access point.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Bucket Keys lower the cost of SSE-KMS by reducing the number of AWS KMS API requests that Amazon S3 makes. They preserve SSE-KMS encryption and can use the existing KMS key, requiring only a bucket configuration change. [Amazon S3 Bucket Keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-key.html)

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Bucket Keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-key.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An errant process is known to consume an entire processor and run at 100%. A CloudOps engineer wants to automate restarting an Amazon EC2 instance when the issue occurs for more than 2 minutes.  
  
How can this be accomplished?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the EC2 instance with basic monitoring. Add an action to restart the instance.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the EC2 instance with detailed monitoring. Add an action to restart the instance.
Create an AWS Lambda function to restart the EC2 instance, invoked on a scheduled basis every 2 minutes.
Create an AWS Lambda function to restart the EC2 instance, invoked by EC2 health checks.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 detailed monitoring publishes CPU utilization metrics at one-minute intervals. A CloudWatch alarm can evaluate two consecutive one-minute CPUUtilization datapoints at the threshold and perform an EC2 reboot action, meeting the requirement to restart the instance after the condition persists for more than two minutes. Basic monitoring publishes CPU utilization at five-minute intervals.

**Learn more:** [Manage detailed monitoring for your EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/manage-detailed-monitoring.html) · [Stop, terminate, reboot, or recover an EC2 instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/UsingAlarmActions.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates multiple Amazon EC2 instances spread across multiple AWS Regions. The company uses AWS Systems Manager tools to manage the EC2 instances. The company must deploy an auditing software package to every instance to record user logins and all actions users perform.  
  
A CloudOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically installs the auditing software on all existing EC2 instances. The solution must also automatically install the auditing software on new EC2 instances when they launch.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Systems Manager Distributor package that includes the auditing software. Store the package in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association in each Region to install the software package on all managed instances in the company's AWS account.

Load the installer for the auditing software into an Amazon S3 bucket. Connect to every instance by using Systems Manager Fleet Manager Remote Desktop. Download the installer by using the AWS CLI. Run the installer manually.

Create an AWS Lambda function that calls the software installer. Merge the auditing software into the Lambda function by using Lambda layers. Run the Lambda function from each instance by using a scheduled Amazon EventBridge rule.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to react to Amazon EC2 RunInstances events. Configure the rule to modify the events to include a step that runs the software installer. Reboot all the instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Distributor packages software for deployment to Systems Manager managed instances. A Systems Manager State Manager association can target all managed instances in the current AWS account and Region, applies initially to existing instances, and is automatically applied to newly managed nodes. Creating that association in every Region therefore covers both the existing multi-Region fleet and newly launched instances.

**Learn more:** [Install or update Distributor packages - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/distributor-working-with-packages-deploy.html) · [Understanding targets and rate controls in State Manager associations - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-state-manager-targets-and-rate-controls.html)

A company needs to ensure that every Amazon EC2 Windows instance launched in an AWS account has a third-party agent installed. The company uses AWS Systems Manager, and the Windows instances are appropriately tagged. The company must deploy periodic updates to the third-party agent as updates become available.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational effort? *(Choose two.)*

options.text: Create a Systems Manager Distributor package for the third-party agent.
Create a Systems Manager OpsItem that includes the tag value for Windows. Attach the Systems Manager inventory to the OpsItem.
Create an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to log in to each instance and to install or update the third-party agent as needed.
Create a Systems Manager State Manager association to run the AWS-RunRemoteScript document Populate the details of the third-party agent package.

Create a Systems Manager State Manager association to run the AWS-ConfigureAWSPackage document. Populate the details of the third-party agent package. Specify instance tags based on the appropriate tag value for Windows.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Distributor packages third-party software for deployment to managed nodes. A State Manager association that runs `AWS-ConfigureAWSPackage`, targets the Windows instance tags, and is scheduled provides automatic installation for matching instances and periodic package updates with minimal administration.

**Learn more:** [Install or update Distributor packages - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/distributor-working-with-packages-deploy.html) · [Create a package in Distributor - AWS Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/distributor-working-with-packages-create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a stateful web application hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with a single target group. The ALB is configured as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Users report intermittent logouts from the web application.  
  
Which combination of actions should a CloudOps engineer take to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change to the least outstanding requests algorithm on the ALB target group,
Configure cookie forwarding in the CloudFront distribution cache behavior.
Configure header forwarding in the CloudFront distribution cache behavior.
Enable group-level stickiness on the ALB listener rule.
Enable sticky sessions on the ALB target group

questions.explanation:
A stateful application needs session affinity so that a user's requests continue to reach the same EC2 target that holds the session state. Enabling sticky sessions on the ALB target group binds a session to a specific target. CloudFront must also forward the relevant cookies to the ALB; otherwise it removes cookies before sending requests to the origin, preventing the ALB from receiving and using its stickiness cookie.

**Learn more:** [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html) · [Cache content based on cookies - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Cookies.html)
